"""Intake: probes every clip, makes a light edit master when needed, and measures everything the line will use."""

from __future__ import annotations

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from ... import media
from .. import analysis as an
from .. import look
from ..model import AgentRun, Clip
from .base import Agent, Ctx, save_jpg


def ingest(ctx: Ctx, clip: Clip, say) -> bool:
    """Measure one clip. Returns False when it was already measured (nothing to do)."""
    npz = ctx.root / "analysis" / f"{clip.id}.npz"
    if clip.analysis and npz.exists() and clip.master and ctx.abs(clip.master).exists():
        return False
    src = ctx.abs(clip.path)
    info = media.probe(src)
    clip.duration, clip.width, clip.height = info["duration"], info["width"], info["height"]
    clip.fps, clip.has_audio = info["fps"] or 30.0, info["has_audio"]
    fps_a = float(min(np.clip(1500 / max(clip.duration, 1), 2, 10), clip.fps))
    size = an.analysis_size(clip.width, clip.height)
    big = max(clip.width, clip.height) > 1920 or info["vcodec"] not in ("h264",)
    if big:
        msize = an.master_size(clip.width, clip.height)
        out = ctx.root / "media" / f"{clip.id}_master.mp4"
        fr = an.master_and_frames(src, out, msize, fps_a, size, clip.fps, clip.has_audio)
        clip.master = ctx.rel(out)
        say(f"{clip.name}: {clip.width}x{clip.height} {info['vcodec']} → {msize[0]}x{msize[1]} edit master "
            f"(1 s keyframes, every cut seeks instantly)")
    else:
        fr = an.frames(src, fps_a, size)
        clip.master = clip.path
    m = an.measure(fr)
    sx, conf = an.subject_track(fr, fps_a)
    sxs = an.smooth(sx, max(3, int(round(fps_a * 1.2))))
    clip.cuts = an.detect_cuts(m["hdist"], m["motion"], fps_a)
    edges = [0.0, *clip.cuts, clip.duration]
    clip.shots = [[round(a, 3), round(b, 3)] for a, b in zip(edges, edges[1:])]
    px = look.pixel_sample(fr)
    st = look.stats(px)
    clip.levels = st
    clip.flat = (st["luma"][4] - st["luma"][0] < 0.75) or st["sat"] < 0.12
    sharp_n = an.norm(m["sharp"])
    quality = sharp_n - np.abs(m["bright"] - 0.45) * 1.2 - 2 * (m["hi"] + m["lo"])
    lo, hi = int(len(quality) * 0.1), max(int(len(quality) * 0.9), int(len(quality) * 0.1) + 1)
    clip.best_t = round(float((lo + int(np.argmax(quality[lo:hi]))) / fps_a), 2) if len(quality) else 0.0
    w = np.clip(conf, 1, None)
    clip.subject = round(float((sxs * w).sum() / w.sum()), 3) if len(sxs) else 0.5
    db = np.zeros(1, np.float32)
    if clip.has_audio:
        db = an.envelope_db(an.pcm(ctx.abs(clip.master), 16000), 16000)
        if float(db.max()) < -55:
            clip.has_audio = False
            say(f"{clip.name}: the audio track is silent; treating the clip as silent")
        else:
            clip.sound = an.sound_regions(db)
    npz.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    step = max(1, len(px) // 40000)
    np.savez_compressed(npz, t=np.arange(len(fr), dtype=np.float32) / fps_a, sharp=m["sharp"], motion=m["motion"],
                        bright=m["bright"], sat=m["sat"], hi=m["hi"], lo=m["lo"], hdist=m["hdist"], rgb=m["rgb"],
                        sx=sxs, sx_raw=sx, conf=conf, px=(px[::step] * 255).astype(np.uint8), th=an.thumbs(fr), db=db)
    clip.analysis, clip.analysis_fps = ctx.rel(npz), round(fps_a, 4)
    stills = ctx.root / "stills"
    media.frame(ctx.abs(clip.master), clip.best_t, stills / f"{clip.id}_poster.jpg", height=360)
    clip.poster = f"stills/{clip.id}_poster.jpg"
    idx = np.linspace(0, len(fr) - 1, 8).astype(int) if len(fr) else []
    if len(idx):
        save_jpg(np.concatenate([fr[i] for i in idx], axis=1), stills / f"{clip.id}_strip.jpg")
        clip.filmstrip = f"stills/{clip.id}_strip.jpg"
    return True


class Intake(Agent):
    key, title, icon, color = "intake", "Intake", "layers", "#7aa2f7"
    role = "probes every clip, builds a light edit master and measures sharpness, motion, exposure, cuts, subject and sound"

    def inputs(self, ctx: Ctx):
        return [(c.id, c.path, c.analysis) for c in ctx.project.clips]

    def run(self, ctx: Ctx, rep: AgentRun) -> None:
        clips = ctx.project.clips
        if not clips:
            raise RuntimeError("no footage: add at least one clip")

        def one(c: Clip) -> bool:
            return ingest(ctx, c, lambda m: self.say(ctx, m))

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex:
            fresh = list(ex.map(one, clips))
        for c, new in zip(clips, fresh):
            lv = c.levels
            bits = [f"{c.width}x{c.height} {c.fps:g} fps {c.duration:.1f}s",
                    f"{len(c.cuts)} camera cut{'s' if len(c.cuts) != 1 else ''}",
                    "flat/log colour" if c.flat else "normal contrast",
                    f"subject around x={c.subject:.2f}",
                    f"{len(c.sound)} sound stretches" if c.has_audio else "no sound"]
            self.decide(ctx, rep, f"{c.id} {c.name}: " + " · ".join(bits) + ("" if new else " (measured earlier)"))
            self.check(ctx, rep, f"{c.id} measured", bool(c.analysis) and lv.get("luma") is not None,
                       f"luma {lv['luma'][0]:.2f}–{lv['luma'][4]:.2f}, saturation {lv['sat']:.2f}")
        total = sum(c.duration for c in clips)
        rep.summary = f"{len(clips)} clip{'s' if len(clips) > 1 else ''}, {total:.1f}s of footage measured"
        rep.preview = clips[0].poster

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
entries.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages
entries.description: Read browser console messages (console.log, console.error, console.warn, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging JavaScript errors, viewing application logs, or understanding what's happening in the browser console. Returns console messages from the current domain only. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs. IMPORTANT: Always provide a pattern to filter messages - without a pattern, you may get too many irrelevant messages.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read console messages from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

onlyErrors.description: If true, only return error and exception messages. Default is false (return all message types).

clear.description: If true, clear the console messages after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to filter console messages. Only messages matching this pattern will be returned (e.g., 'error|warning' to find errors and warnings, 'MyApp' to filter app-specific logs). You should always provide a pattern to avoid getting too many irrelevant messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__resize_window
entries.description: Resize the current browser window to specified dimensions. Useful for testing responsive designs or setting up specific screen sizes. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to get the window for. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
entries.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

entries.description: Execute a sequence of browser tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. toolUseResult.originalFile:
"""Filtergraphs shared by the Export agent (whole segments) and the agents' preview stills (single frames).

One segment = trim → speed → frame-rate → reframe (cover-scale + crop that can pan; perspective for smooth
zoom, punch-ins and gate weave) → colour (the clip's 3D LUT) → RGB effects (halation, glow, vignette...)
→ YUV effects (grain on luma, flicker) → fades and whip blur.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from pathlib import Path

from .agents.base import Ctx, fps_arg
from .look import fx_rgb, fx_yuv
from .model import Clip, Seg


def _even_up(x: float) -> int:
    return int(math.ceil(x / 2) * 2)


def cover(sw: int, sh: int, W: int, H: int, z: float = 1.0) -> tuple[int, int]:
    s = max(W / sw, H / sh) * z
    return _even_up(sw * s), _even_up(sh * s)


def window(clip: Clip, W: int, H: int) -> float:
    """Fraction of the source width that is visible after a cover-crop to W x H (at zoom 1)."""
    return min(1.0, (W / H) / (clip.width / clip.height))


def video_graph(seg: Seg, clip: Clip, W: int, H: int, fps: float, lut: str | None, fx: dict,
                grain: float | None, motion: dict, whip_in: float = 0.0, whip_out: float = 0.0,
                still: bool = False) -> str:
    """Filtergraph from [0:v] to [v] for one clip segment."""
    L = max(seg.length, 1 / fps)
    chain = ["setpts=PTS-STARTPTS"]
    if abs(seg.speed - 1) > 1e-3:
        chain.append(f"setpts=PTS/{seg.speed:.5f}")
    if motion.get("cadence") and not still:
        chain.append(f"fps={int(motion['cadence'])}")
    if not still:
        chain.append(f"fps={fps_arg(fps)}")
    graded = f"format=gbrp,lut3d=file={lut}:interp=tetrahedral" if lut else "format=gbrp"
    parts: list[str] = []
    if seg.fill in ("blur", "fit"):
        parts.append(f"[0:v]{','.join(chain)},{graded},split[bgs][fgs]")
        if seg.fill == "blur":
            parts.append(f"[bgs]scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop={W}:{H},"
                         f"gblur=sigma={min(W, H) * 0.045:.1f},colorlevels=romax=0.8:gomax=0.8:bomax=0.8[bg]")
        else:
            parts.append(f"[bgs]scale={W}:{H},colorlevels=romax=0:gomax=0:bomax=0[bg]")
        parts.append(f"[fgs]scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease:flags=lanczos[fg]")
        parts.append("[bg][fg]overlay=(W-w)/2:(H-h)/2[in]")
    else:
        z0, z1 = max(seg.zoom0, 1.0), max(seg.zoom1, 1.0)
        zs = min(z0, z1)
        cw, ch = cover(clip.width, clip.height, W, H, zs)
        xa = min(max(seg.x0 * cw - W / 2, 0), cw - W)
        xb = min(max(seg.x1 * cw - W / 2, 0), cw - W)
        y = (ch - H) // 2
        if abs(xb - xa) < 1:
            crop = f"crop={W}:{H}:x={int(xa)}:y={y}"
        else:
            crop = f"crop={W}:{H}:x='{xa:.1f}+({xb - xa:.1f})*min(t/{L:.3f},1)':y={y}"
        steps = [*chain, f"scale={cw}:{ch}:flags=lanczos", crop]
        r0, r1 = z0 / zs, z1 / zs
        weave = float(motion.get("weave") or 0)
        if abs(r0 - 1) > 1e-3 or abs(r1 - 1) > 1e-3 or weave:
            tt = f"(in/{fps:.4f})"
            if seg.zoom_ease == "punch":
                r = f"({r1:.4f}+({r0 - r1:.4f})*pow(max(0,1-{tt}/0.28),2))"
            else:
                r = f"({r0:.4f}+({r1 - r0:.4f})*min({tt}/{L:.3f},1))"
            dx = dy = "0"
            if weave:
                a = weave * W / 1080
                r = f"(1.04*{r})"
                dx = f"({a:.2f}*(sin({tt}*5.3)+0.6*sin({tt}*11.1+1.3)))"
                dy = f"({a * 0.7:.2f}*(sin({tt}*4.1+0.7)+0.5*sin({tt}*9.7)))"
            hw, hh = f"(W/(2*{r}))", f"(H/(2*{r}))"
            cx, cy = f"(W/2+{dx})", f"(H/2+{dy})"
            steps.append(f"perspective=x0='{cx}-{hw}':y0='{cy}-{hh}':x1='{cx}+{hw}':y1='{cy}-{hh}':"
                         f"x2='{cx}-{hw}':y2='{cy}+{hh}':x3='{cx}+{hw}':y3='{cy}+{hh}':interpolation=linear:eval=frame")
        steps.append(graded)
        parts.append(f"[0:v]{','.join(steps)}[in]")
    rgb = fx_rgb(fx, W, H)
    parts.append(rgb)
    tail = ["scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv", "format=yuv420p", "setsar=1", *fx_yuv(fx, grain, min(W, H))]
    if not still:
        if seg.fade_in > 0:
            tail.append(f"fade=t=in:st=0:d={seg.fade_in:.3f}")
        if seg.fade_out > 0:
            tail.append(f"fade=t=out:st={max(L - seg.fade_out, 0):.3f}:d={seg.fade_out:.3f}")
        radius = max(8, round(W * 0.05))
        if whip_in:
            tail.append(f"dblur=angle=0:radius={radius}:enable='lt(t,{whip_in:.3f})'")
        if whip_out:
            tail.append(f"dblur=angle=0:radius={radius}:enable='gt(t,{L - whip_out:.3f})'")
    parts.append(f"[out]{','.join(tail)}[v]")
    return ";".join(parts)


def card_graph(seg: Seg, W: int, H: int, fps: float) -> list[str]:
    return ["-f", "lavfi", "-i", f"color=c=black:s={W}x{H}:r={fps_arg(fps)}:d={seg.length:.4f}"]


def render_segment(ctx: Ctx, seg: Seg, clip: Clip | None, W: int, H: int, fps: float, lut: str | None,
                   fx: dict, grain: float | None, motion: dict, out: Path, whip_in: float = 0.0,
                   whip_out: float = 0.0) -> Path:
    enc = ["-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "15", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-color_primaries", "bt709",
           "-color_trc", "bt709", "-colorspace", "bt709", "-an", "-r", fps_arg(fps), "-t", f"{seg.length:.4f}"]
    if seg.kind == "card" or clip is None:
        ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", *card_graph(seg, W, H, fps), "-vf", "format=yuv420p", *enc, ctx.rel(out)])
        return out
    span = seg.src_out - seg.src_in
    graph = video_graph(seg, clip, W, H, fps, lut, fx, grain, motion, whip_in, whip_out)
    ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", "-ss", f"{seg.src_in:.4f}", "-t", f"{span + 0.1:.4f}", "-i", clip.master,
                "-filter_complex", graph, "-map", "[v]", *enc, ctx.rel(out)])
    return out


def still(ctx: Ctx, clip: Clip, t: float, out: Path, W: int, H: int, lut: str | None = None, fx: dict | None = None,
          grain: float | None = None, x: float | None = None, zoom: float = 1.0, ass: str | None = None,
          ass_t: float = 0.0, fill: str = "crop") -> Path:
    """One graded frame, framed exactly like the render (for the agents' previews and the look gallery)."""
    seg = Seg(id=0, clip=clip.id, src_in=t, src_out=t + 0.04, x0=x if x is not None else clip.subject,
              x1=x if x is not None else clip.subject, zoom0=zoom, zoom1=zoom, fill=fill)
    graph = video_graph(seg, clip, W, H, 25.0, lut, fx or {}, grain, {}, still=True)
    if ass:
        graph = graph[: graph.rfind("[v]")] + f",setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+{ass_t:.3f}/TB,subtitles={ass}:fontsdir=render/fonts[v]"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", "-ss", f"{max(t, 0):.3f}", "-i", clip.master, "-filter_complex", graph, "-map", "[v]",
                "-frames:v", "1", "-q:v", "3", ctx.rel(out)])
    return out

toolUseResult.originalFile:
"""Filtergraphs shared by the Export agent (whole segments) and the agents' preview stills (single frames).

One segment = trim → speed → frame-rate → reframe (cover-scale + crop that can pan; perspective for smooth
zoom, punch-ins and gate weave) → colour (the clip's 3D LUT) → RGB effects (halation, glow, vignette...)
→ YUV effects (grain on luma, flicker) → fades and whip blur.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from pathlib import Path

from .agents.base import Ctx, fps_arg
from .look import fx_rgb, fx_yuv
from .model import Clip, Seg


def _even_up(x: float) -> int:
    return int(math.ceil(x / 2) * 2)


def cover(sw: int, sh: int, W: int, H: int, z: float = 1.0) -> tuple[int, int]:
    s = max(W / sw, H / sh) * z
    return _even_up(sw * s), _even_up(sh * s)


def window(clip: Clip, W: int, H: int) -> float:
    """Fraction of the source width that is visible after a cover-crop to W x H (at zoom 1)."""
    return min(1.0, (W / H) / (clip.width / clip.height))


def video_graph(seg: Seg, clip: Clip, W: int, H: int, fps: float, lut: str | None, fx: dict,
                grain: float | None, motion: dict, whip_in: float = 0.0, whip_out: float = 0.0,
                still: bool = False) -> str:
    """Filtergraph from [0:v] to [v] for one clip segment."""
    L = max(seg.length, 1 / fps)
    chain = ["setpts=PTS-STARTPTS"]
    if abs(seg.speed - 1) > 1e-3:
        chain.append(f"setpts=PTS/{seg.speed:.5f}")
    if motion.get("cadence") and not still:
        chain.append(f"fps={int(motion['cadence'])}")
    if not still:
        chain.append(f"fps={fps_arg(fps)}")
    graded = f"format=gbrp,lut3d=file={lut}:interp=tetrahedral" if lut else "format=gbrp"
    parts: list[str] = []
    if seg.fill in ("blur", "fit"):
        parts.append(f"[0:v]{','.join(chain)},{graded},split[bgs][fgs]")
        if seg.fill == "blur":
            parts.append(f"[bgs]scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop={W}:{H},"
                         f"gblur=sigma={min(W, H) * 0.045:.1f},colorlevels=romax=0.8:gomax=0.8:bomax=0.8[bg]")
        else:
            parts.append(f"[bgs]scale={W}:{H},colorlevels=romax=0:gomax=0:bomax=0[bg]")
        parts.append(f"[fgs]scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease:flags=lanczos[fg]")
        parts.append("[bg][fg]overlay=(W-w)/2:(H-h)/2[in]")
    else:
        z0, z1 = max(seg.zoom0, 1.0), max(seg.zoom1, 1.0)
        zs = min(z0, z1)
        # Crop the window in source pixels first, then scale only that up to the frame: far less work than
        # scaling the whole source to cover the frame and throwing most of it away.
        if clip.width / clip.height >= W / H:
            cw, ch = f"ih*{W / H:.6f}/{zs:.4f}", f"ih/{zs:.4f}"
        else:
            cw, ch = f"iw/{zs:.4f}", f"iw*{H / W:.6f}/{zs:.4f}"
        if abs(seg.x1 - seg.x0) < 1e-3:
            cx = f"{seg.x0:.4f}"
        else:
            cx = f"({seg.x0:.4f}+({seg.x1 - seg.x0:.4f})*min(t/{L:.3f},1))"
        crop = (f"crop=w='trunc({cw}/2)*2':h='trunc({ch}/2)*2':x='clip({cx}*iw-ow/2,0,iw-ow)':y='(ih-oh)/2'")
        steps = [*chain, crop, f"scale={W}:{H}:flags=lanczos"]
        r0, r1 = z0 / zs, z1 / zs
        weave = float(motion.get("weave") or 0)
        if abs(r0 - 1) > 1e-3 or abs(r1 - 1) > 1e-3 or weave:
            tt = f"(in/{fps:.4f})"
            if seg.zoom_ease == "punch":
                r = f"({r1:.4f}+({r0 - r1:.4f})*pow(max(0,1-{tt}/0.28),2))"
            else:
                r = f"({r0:.4f}+({r1 - r0:.4f})*min({tt}/{L:.3f},1))"
            dx = dy = "0"
            if weave:
                a = weave * W / 1080
                r = f"(1.04*{r})"
                dx = f"({a:.2f}*(sin({tt}*5.3)+0.6*sin({tt}*11.1+1.3)))"
                dy = f"({a * 0.7:.2f}*(sin({tt}*4.1+0.7)+0.5*sin({tt}*9.7)))"
            hw, hh = f"(W/(2*{r}))", f"(H/(2*{r}))"
            cx, cy = f"(W/2+{dx})", f"(H/2+{dy})"
            steps.append(f"perspective=x0='{cx}-{hw}':y0='{cy}-{hh}':x1='{cx}+{hw}':y1='{cy}-{hh}':"
                         f"x2='{cx}-{hw}':y2='{cy}+{hh}':x3='{cx}+{hw}':y3='{cy}+{hh}':interpolation=linear:eval=frame")
        steps.append(graded)
        parts.append(f"[0:v]{','.join(steps)}[in]")
    rgb = fx_rgb(fx, W, H)
    parts.append(rgb)
    tail = ["scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv", "format=yuv420p", "setsar=1", *fx_yuv(fx, grain, min(W, H))]
    if not still:
        if seg.fade_in > 0:
            tail.append(f"fade=t=in:st=0:d={seg.fade_in:.3f}")
        if seg.fade_out > 0:
            tail.append(f"fade=t=out:st={max(L - seg.fade_out, 0):.3f}:d={seg.fade_out:.3f}")
        radius = max(8, round(W * 0.05))
        if whip_in:
            tail.append(f"dblur=angle=0:radius={radius}:enable='lt(t,{whip_in:.3f})'")
        if whip_out:
            tail.append(f"dblur=angle=0:radius={radius}:enable='gt(t,{L - whip_out:.3f})'")
    parts.append(f"[out]{','.join(tail)}[v]")
    return ";".join(parts)


def card_graph(seg: Seg, W: int, H: int, fps: float) -> list[str]:
    return ["-f", "lavfi", "-i", f"color=c=black:s={W}x{H}:r={fps_arg(fps)}:d={seg.length:.4f}"]


def render_segment(ctx: Ctx, seg: Seg, clip: Clip | None, W: int, H: int, fps: float, lut: str | None,
                   fx: dict, grain: float | None, motion: dict, out: Path, whip_in: float = 0.0,
                   whip_out: float = 0.0) -> Path:
    enc = ["-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "15", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-color_primaries", "bt709",
           "-color_trc", "bt709", "-colorspace", "bt709", "-an", "-r", fps_arg(fps), "-t", f"{seg.length:.4f}"]
    if seg.kind == "card" or clip is None:
        ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", *card_graph(seg, W, H, fps), "-vf", "format=yuv420p", *enc, ctx.rel(out)])
        return out
    span = seg.src_out - seg.src_in
    graph = video_graph(seg, clip, W, H, fps, lut, fx, grain, motion, whip_in, whip_out)
    ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", "-ss", f"{seg.src_in:.4f}", "-t", f"{span + 0.1:.4f}", "-i", clip.master,
                "-filter_complex", graph, "-map", "[v]", *enc, ctx.rel(out)])
    return out


def still(ctx: Ctx, clip: Clip, t: float, out: Path, W: int, H: int, lut: str | None = None, fx: dict | None = None,
          grain: float | None = None, x: float | None = None, zoom: float = 1.0, ass: str | None = None,
          ass_t: float = 0.0, fill: str = "crop") -> Path:
    """One graded frame, framed exactly like the render (for the agents' previews and the look gallery)."""
    seg = Seg(id=0, clip=clip.id, src_in=t, src_out=t + 0.04, x0=x if x is not None else clip.subject,
              x1=x if x is not None else clip.subject, zoom0=zoom, zoom1=zoom, fill=fill)
    graph = video_graph(seg, clip, W, H, 25.0, lut, fx or {}, grain, {}, still=True)
    if ass:
        graph = graph[: graph.rfind("[v]")] + f",setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+{ass_t:.3f}/TB,subtitles={ass}:fontsdir=render/fonts[v]"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", "-ss", f"{max(t, 0):.3f}", "-i", clip.master, "-filter_complex", graph, "-map", "[v]",
                "-frames:v", "1", "-q:v", "3", ctx.rel(out)])
    return out

def video_graph(seg: Seg, clip: Clip, W: int, H: int, fps: float, lut: str | None, fx: dict,
                grain: float | None, motion: dict, whip_in: float = 0.0, whip_out: float = 0.0,
                still: bool = False) -> str:
    """Filtergraph from [0:v] to [v] for one clip segment."""
    L = max(seg.length, 1 / fps)
    chain = ["setpts=PTS-STARTPTS"]
    if abs(seg.speed - 1) > 1e-3:
        chain.append(f"setpts=PTS/{seg.speed:.5f}")
    if motion.get("cadence") and not still:
        chain.append(f"fps={int(motion['cadence'])}")
    if not still:
        chain.append(f"fps={fps_arg(fps)}")
    graded = f"format=gbrp,lut3d=file={lut}:interp=tetrahedral" if lut else "format=gbrp"
    parts: list[str] = []
    if seg.fill in ("blur", "fit"):
        parts.append(f"[0:v]{','.join(chain)},{graded},split[bgs][fgs]")
        if seg.fill == "blur":
            parts.append(f"[bgs]scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop={W}:{H},"
                         f"gblur=sigma={min(W, H) * 0.045:.1f},colorlevels=romax=0.8:gomax=0.8:bomax=0.8[bg]")
        else:
            parts.append(f"[bgs]scale={W}:{H},colorlevels=romax=0:gomax=0:bomax=0[bg]")
        parts.append(f"[fgs]scale={W}:{H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease:flags=lanczos[fg]")
        parts.append("[bg][fg]overlay=(W-w)/2:(H-h)/2[in]")
    else:
        z0, z1 = max(seg.zoom0, 1.0), max(seg.zoom1, 1.0)
        zs = min(z0, z1)
        # Crop the window in source pixels first, then scale only that up to the frame: far less work than
        # scaling the whole source to cover the frame and throwing most of it away.
        if clip.width / clip.height >= W / H:
            cw, ch = f"ih*{W / H:.6f}/{zs:.4f}", f"ih/{zs:.4f}"
        else:
            cw, ch = f"iw/{zs:.4f}", f"iw*{H / W:.6f}/{zs:.4f}"
        if abs(seg.x1 - seg.x0) < 1e-3:
            cx = f"{seg.x0:.4f}"
        else:
            cx = f"({seg.x0:.4f}+({seg.x1 - seg.x0:.4f})*min(t/{L:.3f},1))"
        crop = (f"crop=w='trunc({cw}/2)*2':h='trunc({ch}/2)*2':x='clip({cx}*iw-ow/2,0,iw-ow)':y='(ih-oh)/2'")
        steps = [*chain, crop]
        r0, r1 = z0 / zs, z1 / zs
        weave = float(motion.get("weave") or 0)
        if abs(r0 - 1) > 1e-3 or abs(r1 - 1) > 1e-3 or weave:
            # zoom / weave at source resolution (before the upscale): same look, a fraction of the pixels
            tt = f"(in/{fps:.4f})"
            if seg.zoom_ease == "punch":
                r = f"({r1:.4f}+({r0 - r1:.4f})*pow(max(0,1-{tt}/0.28),2))"
            else:
                r = f"({r0:.4f}+({r1 - r0:.4f})*min({tt}/{L:.3f},1))"
            dx = dy = "0"
            if weave:
                a = weave / 1080
                r = f"(1.04*{r})"
                dx = f"({a:.5f}*W*(sin({tt}*5.3)+0.6*sin({tt}*11.1+1.3)))"
                dy = f"({a * 0.7:.5f}*W*(sin({tt}*4.1+0.7)+0.5*sin({tt}*9.7)))"
            hw, hh = f"(W/(2*{r}))", f"(H/(2*{r}))"
            cx, cy = f"(W/2+{dx})", f"(H/2+{dy})"
            steps.append(f"perspective=x0='{cx}-{hw}':y0='{cy}-{hh}':x1='{cx}+{hw}':y1='{cy}-{hh}':"
                         f"x2='{cx}-{hw}':y2='{cy}+{hh}':x3='{cx}+{hw}':y3='{cy}+{hh}':interpolation=linear:eval=frame")
        # grade at source resolution too, then one upscale to the frame
        steps += [graded.replace("tetrahedral", "trilinear"), f"scale={W}:{H}:flags=lanczos"]
        parts.append(f"[0:v]{','.join(steps)}[in]")
    rgb = fx_rgb(fx, W, H)
    parts.append(rgb)
    tail = ["scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv", "format=yuv420p", "setsar=1", *fx_yuv(fx, grain, min(W, H))]
    if not still:
        if seg.fade_in > 0:
            tail.append(f"fade=t=in:st=0:d={seg.fade_in:.3f}")
        if seg.fade_out > 0:
            tail.append(f"fade=t=out:st={max(L - seg.fade_out, 0):.3f}:d={seg.fade_out:.3f}")
        radius = max(8, round(W * 0.05))
        if whip_in:
            tail.append(f"dblur=angle=0:radius={radius}:enable='lt(t,{whip_in:.3f})'")
        if whip_out:
            tail.append(f"dblur=angle=0:radius={radius}:enable='gt(t,{L - whip_out:.3f})'")
    parts.append(f"[out]{','.join(tail)}[v]")
    return ";".join(parts)


def card_graph(seg: Seg, W: int, H: int, fps: float) -> list[str]:
    return ["-f", "lavfi", "-i", f"color=c=black:s={W}x{H}:r={fps_arg(fps)}:d={seg.length:.4f}"]


def render_segment(ctx: Ctx, seg: Seg, clip: Clip | None, W: int, H: int, fps: float, lut: str | None,
                   fx: dict, grain: float | None, motion: dict, out: Path, whip_in: float = 0.0,
                   whip_out: float = 0.0) -> Path:
    enc = ["-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "15", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-color_primaries", "bt709",
           "-color_trc", "bt709", "-colorspace", "bt709", "-an", "-r", fps_arg(fps), "-t", f"{seg.length:.4f}"]
    if seg.kind == "card" or clip is None:
        ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", *card_graph(seg, W, H, fps), "-vf", "format=yuv420p", *enc, ctx.rel(out)])

"""Filtergraphs shared by the Export agent (whole segments) and the agents' preview stills (single frames).

One segment = trim → speed → frame-rate → reframe (cover-scale + crop that can pan; perspective for smooth
zoom, punch-ins and gate weave) → colour (the clip's 3D LUT) → RGB effects (halation, glow, vignette...)
→ YUV effects (grain on luma, flicker) → fades and whip blur.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from pathlib import Path

from .agents.base import Ctx, fps_arg
from .look import fx_rgb, fx_yuv
from .model import Clip, Seg


def _even_up(x: float) -> int:
    return int(math.ceil(x / 2) * 2)


def cover(sw: int, sh: int, W: int, H: int, z: float = 1.0) -> tuple[int, int]:
    s = max(W / sw, H / sh) * z
    return _even_up(sw * s), _even_up(sh * s)


def window(clip: Clip, W: int, H: int) -> float:
    """Fraction of the source width that is visible after a cover-crop to W x H (at zoom 1)."""
    return min(1.0, (W / H) / (clip.width / clip.height))


def video_graph(seg: Seg, clip: Clip, W: int, H: int, fps: float, lut: str | None, fx: dict,
                grain: float | None, motion: dict, whip_in: float = 0.0, whip_out: float = 0.0,
                still: bool = False) -> str:
    """Filtergraph from [0:v] to [v] for one clip segment."""
    L = max(seg.length, 1 / fps)
    chain = ["setpts=PTS-STARTPTS"]
    if abs(seg.speed - 1) > 1e-3:
        chain.append(f"setpts=PTS/{seg.speed:.5f}")
    if motion.get("cadence") and not still:
        chain.append(f"fps={int(motion['cadence'])}")
    if not still:
        chain.append(f"fps={fps_arg(fps)}")
    graded = f"format=gbrp,lut3d=file={lut}:interp=tetrahedral" if lut else "format=gbrp"
    parts: list[str] = []
    if seg.fill in ("blur", "fit"):
        parts.append(f"[0:v]{','.join(chain)},{graded},split[bgs][fgs]")

        if whip_in:
            tail.append(f"dblur=angle=0:radius={radius}:enable='lt(t,{whip_in:.3f})'")
        if whip_out:
            tail.append(f"dblur=angle=0:radius={radius}:enable='gt(t,{L - whip_out:.3f})'")
    parts.append(f"[out]{','.join(tail)}[v]")
    return ";".join(parts)


def card_graph(seg: Seg, W: int, H: int, fps: float) -> list[str]:
    return ["-f", "lavfi", "-i", f"color=c=black:s={W}x{H}:r={fps_arg(fps)}:d={seg.length:.4f}"]


def render_segment(ctx: Ctx, seg: Seg, clip: Clip | None, W: int, H: int, fps: float, lut: str | None,
                   fx: dict, grain: float | None, motion: dict, out: Path, whip_in: float = 0.0,
                   whip_out: float = 0.0) -> Path:
    enc = ["-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "15", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-color_primaries", "bt709",
           "-color_trc", "bt709", "-colorspace", "bt709", "-an", "-r", fps_arg(fps), "-t", f"{seg.length:.4f}"]
    if seg.kind == "card" or clip is None:
        ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", *card_graph(seg, W, H, fps), "-vf", "format=yuv420p", *enc, ctx.rel(out)])
        return out
    span = seg.src_out - seg.src_in
    graph = video_graph(seg, clip, W, H, fps, lut, fx, grain, motion, whip_in, whip_out)
    ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", "-ss", f"{seg.src_in:.4f}", "-t", f"{span + 0.1:.4f}", "-i", clip.master,
                "-filter_complex", graph, "-map", "[v]", *enc, ctx.rel(out)])
    return out


def still(ctx: Ctx, clip: Clip, t: float, out: Path, W: int, H: int, lut: str | None = None, fx: dict | None = None,
          grain: float | None = None, x: float | None = None, zoom: float = 1.0, ass: str | None = None,
          ass_t: float = 0.0, fill: str = "crop") -> Path:
    """One graded frame, framed exactly like the render (for the agents' previews and the look gallery)."""
    seg = Seg(id=0, clip=clip.id, src_in=t, src_out=t + 0.04, x0=x if x is not None else clip.subject,
              x1=x if x is not None else clip.subject, zoom0=zoom, zoom1=zoom, fill=fill)
    graph = video_graph(seg, clip, W, H, 25.0, lut, fx or {}, grain, {}, still=True)
    if ass:
        graph = graph[: graph.rfind("[v]")] + f",setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+{ass_t:.3f}/TB,subtitles={ass}:fontsdir=render/fonts[v]"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ctx.ffmpeg(["-y", "-ss", f"{max(t, 0):.3f}", "-i", clip.master, "-filter_complex", graph, "-map", "[v]",
                "-frames:v", "1", "-q:v", "3", ctx.rel(out)])
    return out

name: cutroom-direction
description: Cutroom must be a deterministic multi-agent video editor with a UI and selectable creative skills, not an LLM reel maker

Cutroom (E:\desktop folders\hackathonS\cutroom) is an agentic video EDITOR with a full UI ("Cutroom Studio"), not a reel maker.
The user rejected the LLM-driven brief→reel pipeline ("THIS IS SHIT WE ARE NOT MAKING ANY REEL MAKER").

**Why:** they want editing done by code (no model in the edit path), in the style of their reference creators (bonzo / @Wordisbonz first),
with the user choosing format, details and look, and a reference video analysed first and matched.

**How to apply:**
- Editing styles are "skills" (bonzo, confessional, roaming, trailer, beatcut, super8, dreamy, clean) the user picks; a reference video overrides rhythm/colour.
- Fixed-role agents run as an assembly line (intake, reference, music, colorist, cutter, reframer, motion, typographer, mixer, export, QA), parallel where independent, cached when inputs are unchanged.
- Use the hackathon tools where useful (neatlogs spans per agent, Entire checkpoints); don't add Gemini/Groq into the edit path.
- Judge output by looking at rendered frames; keep the UI polished (they asked for "the best UI").
Related: [[hackathon-neathack]]

# Cutroom

**An AI post-production team you can hand raw footage and a one-line brief, and walk away.**
A logger watches every clip, a producer writes the spec, an editor agent cuts it with real editing tools, a motion
designer makes the titles and thumbnail, and a critic watches every draft and sends it back until it's good enough to
post. Every render is measured (length, black and frozen frames, loudness, pacing, caption speed), every decision is
traced in [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com), and a crash resumes mid-edit.

```
$ cutroom make "30s vertical teaser for Reels: open on the robot attack, best dialogue with captions, end on the title" \
    footage/tears-of-steel/*.mov
```

Outputs: `final.mp4` (9:16, word-by-word captions, animated titles, loudness-normalised to −14 LUFS), `thumbnail.png`,
`captions.srt`, and an **edit sheet** (`index.html`): the cut list with a frame per segment, every quality check, and
the creative director's notes, round by round.

> Built for #neatHack 2026 ("Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching"). Work in progress.

## The team

| Agent | What it decides | What keeps it honest |
|---|---|---|
| **Logger** | Watches each clip (Gemini video understanding on a 360p proxy) and logs it shot by shot: description, energy, quality, usefulness, highlights | Shot boundaries snapped to FFmpeg scene changes; words and timings come from Whisper, not from the model; if no vision model is available it logs from scene cuts + transcript and the edit continues |
| **Producer** | Platform, aspect ratio, target length, hook, structure, captions, titles, house style | Target length clamped to what the footage can actually fill |
| **Editor** (tool-calling loop) | Every cut: `list_shots`, `read_transcript`, `add_segment`, `trim_segment`, `move_segment`, `set_zoom`, `set_captions`, `add_title`, `preview`, `render_draft`, `finish` | Times must exist in the source; cuts that land mid-word are flagged with the nearest clean point; the running duration and pacing are shown after every action; `finish` is refused until the current timeline is rendered and its checks pass |
| **Motion designer** | Title cards, lower thirds, end cards, thumbnail | HTML/CSS templates rendered to transparent PNGs and animated by FFmpeg, in the house style |
| **Critic** | Watches the rendered draft like a creative director: hook, pacing, story, legibility, anything broken; approve or revise with up to 4 concrete fixes | Measurable checks run on every render; approval needs a score ≥ 7 |

## Taste without fine-tuning: learn a creator's style from their public videos

```
cutroom style learn --name bonzo --url https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sKdC4Bs-cKA --url https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tonG-OufefQ
```

A vision model watches windows of the creator's **public** videos through Gemini's own YouTube-URL input (nothing is
downloaded or re-used) and reports, in a fixed structure: the time of every cut, every piece of on-screen text (words,
case, position, size, font feel), the look (temperature, contrast, saturation, black level, grain, vignette,
letterbox), camera, transitions and speed changes, sound (voice-over vs to-camera, music role, cuts on the beat), how
the video opens and is built, and its signature moves. Cutroom turns that into a **style profile** the renderer can
execute and the critic can measure against: shot rhythm, a concrete grade, the text treatment, the story structure.

Profiles learned from the references this project was asked to edit like:

| Profile | Learned signature |
|---|---|
| `bonzo` (@Wordisbonz, "turning my life into short movies") | the story told in bold lowercase text lines; time/place stamps; long handheld walk-and-talk takes with occasional whip-pan bursts; warm, soft, lightly grained look; centred serif title cards on black |
| `farza` (@farzatv) | direct-to-camera confessional; tight jump cuts that remove every pause inside a take; handheld selfie framing that drifts to B-roll; no text, no music |
| `mayv` (@mayv_music) | handheld roaming documentary; location stamps; phrase-by-phrase lowercase subtitles; rapid hard cuts on the beat in music sections |

Only the style is learned. The editor writes its own lines about *your* footage; lines copied from the reference
creator are refused, and the raw observations (which quote the creators' on-screen text) stay out of the repo. Cut
timings come from a vision model sampling 3 frames a second, so rhythm is an estimate (two models disagreed by 3x on
one creator; the stronger model's reading is used).

For local reference videos you have the right to analyse, `cutroom style learn <files> --name x` measures them
directly with FFmpeg instead (shot-length distribution, brightness/saturation, loudness, words per second).

## What the editor can do

Cuts and trims, **jump cuts that strip pauses out of talking footage** (alternating a subtle punch-in to hide them),
slow motion and speed changes, dip-to-black, punch-in zooms, **subject-aware reframing** to vertical, word-by-word or
minimal lowercase captions, **story text and time/place stamps**, title and end cards, music ducked under speech, and a
**film look** per style (colour temperature, lifted or crushed blacks, vignette, grain, letterbox). Flat/log footage gets
an automatic **primary colour correction** (levels stretch, mid-tone and saturation recovery) before the creative look,
and anything over 1080p is edited from an optimised 1080p master.

## Demo footage

The demos use Blender Foundation open movies (*Tears of Steel*, *Sintel*), CC BY 3.0. See `footage/README.md`.

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import numpy as np

from .. import analysis as an
from .. import look, skills
from ..model import AgentRun, Clip
from ..render import still
from .base import Agent, Ctx, frame_size, load_analysis


def clip_pixels(ctx: Ctx, clip: Clip) -> np.ndarray:
    return load_analysis(ctx, clip)["px"].astype(np.float32) / 255.0


def look_params(ctx: Ctx, skill: dict | None = None) -> tuple[dict, float, dict | None]:
    """(look, strength, reference match) for a skill under the current settings."""
    sk = skill or ctx.skill
    strength = float(ctx.settings.look) * float(sk.get("look_strength_scale", 1.0))
    strength *= float(ctx.hints.get("colorist", {}).get("boost_look", 1.0))
    ref = ctx.project.reference
    match = None
    if ref and ref.profile and ctx.settings.match_reference and skill is None:
        px = np.concatenate([look.apply_primary(clip_pixels(ctx, c), look.primary_params(clip_pixels(ctx, c)))
                             for c in ctx.project.clips])
        st = look.stats(px)
        s = min(1.0, float(ctx.settings.reference_strength) + float(ctx.hints.get("colorist", {}).get("boost_ref", 0)))
        match = {"src": st, "ref": ref.profile["look"], "strength": s}
    return sk.get("look") or {}, strength, match


def lut_for(ctx: Ctx, clip: Clip, lk: dict, strength: float, match: dict | None, tag: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    px = clip_pixels(ctx, clip)
    prim = look.primary_params(px)
    key = hashlib.sha1(json.dumps([prim, lk, strength, match], sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:10]
    rel = f"looks/{clip.id}_{tag}_{key}.cube"
    if not ctx.abs(rel).exists():
        look.write_cube(ctx.abs(rel), look.bake(look.grade_fn(prim, lk, strength, match)), title=f"cutroom {tag} {clip.id}")
    return rel, prim


def grain_for(ctx: Ctx, fx: dict) -> float | None:
    if ctx.settings.grain is not None:
        return float(ctx.settings.grain)
    ref = ctx.project.reference
    if ref and ref.profile and ctx.settings.match_reference and ref.profile.get("noise") is not None:
        c = ctx.project.clips[0]
        full = an.frames(ctx.abs(c.master), 6 / max(c.duration, 1), an.analysis_size(c.width, c.height, 960))
        src = an.noise_level(full[:6])
        add = max(float(ref.profile["noise"]) ** 2 - src ** 2, 0) ** 0.5
        return round(float(np.clip(add * 1.73, 0, 22)), 1)
    return float(fx.get("grain", 0))


def look_previews(ctx: Ctx) -> dict[str, str]:
    """A still of the hero clip in every skill's look (and the reference's), for the skill gallery."""
    if not ctx.project.clips:
        return {}
    hero = ctx.project.clips[0]
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    jobs = []
    all_sk = skills.all_skills()
    for name, sk in all_sk.items():
        lk = sk.get("look") or {}
        jobs.append((name, lk, 1.0, None, sk.get("fx") or {}))
    ref = ctx.project.reference
    if ref and ref.profile:
        px = np.concatenate([look.apply_primary(clip_pixels(ctx, c), look.primary_params(clip_pixels(ctx, c)))

        path = ctx.root / "stills" / f"look_{name}.jpg"

        if match:
            self.decide(ctx, rep, f"matching the reference's colour at {match['strength']:.0%} (CIELAB mean + spread transfer); "

        else:

                                  + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in lk.items() if not isinstance(v, list)))
        fx = dict(ctx.skill.get("fx") or {})
        grain = grain_for(ctx, fx)
        if match and ctx.project.reference.profile.get("vignette") is not None:
            fx["vignette"] = ctx.project.reference.profile["vignette"]
        self.decide(ctx, rep, "texture: " + ", ".join([f"grain {grain:g}"] + [f"{k} {v}" for k, v in fx.items() if k != "grain"]))
        for c in p.clips:
            g = graded[c.id]

            self.check(ctx, rep, f"{c.id} exposure", 0.2 <= g["luma"][2] <= 0.66, f"mid-grey {g['luma'][2]:.2f}")
        if match:
            ref_lab = ctx.project.reference.profile["look"]["lab_mean"]
            de = float(np.mean([look.delta_e(graded[c.id]["lab_mean"], ref_lab) for c in p.clips]))
            self.check(ctx, rep, "matches the reference", de < 8, f"average colour ΔE {de:.1f} from the reference (under 8 passes)",
                       hint={"boost_ref": 0.15})
        p.look = {"luts": luts, "primary": prims, "fx": fx, "grain": grain, "strength": strength, "graded": graded,
                  "match": bool(match)}
        hero = p.clips[0]
        W, H = frame_size(ctx.settings)
        scale = 540 / max(W, H)
        sw, sh = round(W * scale / 2) * 2, round(H * scale / 2) * 2
        still(ctx, hero, hero.best_t, ctx.root / "stills" / "colorist_before.jpg", sw, sh)
        still(ctx, hero, hero.best_t, ctx.root / "stills" / "colorist_after.jpg", sw, sh, lut=luts[hero.id], fx=fx, grain=grain)
        rep.before, rep.preview = "stills/colorist_before.jpg", "stills/colorist_after.jpg"
        rep.summary = (f"{len(p.clips)} LUT{'s' if len(p.clips) > 1 else ''} · "
                       + ("reference colour" if match else f"{ctx.skill.get('label')} look") + f" · grain {grain:g}")

"""Offline tests for the studio's algorithms (no network, no models).

Run: uv run python tests/test_studio.py
"""

import sys
import tempfile
import wave
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from cutroom.studio import analysis as an  # noqa: E402
from cutroom.studio import look  # noqa: E402
from cutroom.studio.agents.cutter import NEG, assign_story, plan_beats, plan_free  # noqa: E402
from cutroom.studio.agents.typographer import ass_document  # noqa: E402
from cutroom.studio.model import Text  # noqa: E402


def test_beat_tracker_finds_the_tempo():
    sr, bpm, secs = 22050, 100.0, 30
    y = np.zeros(sr * secs, np.float32)
    period = 60 / bpm
    for k in range(int(secs / period)):
        i = int(k * period * sr)
        n = np.arange(int(0.03 * sr))
        y[i:i + len(n)] += np.sin(2 * np.pi * 120 * n / sr) * np.exp(-n / (0.006 * sr)) * (1.0 if k % 4 == 0 else 0.6)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        path = Path(d) / "clicks.wav"
        with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as w:

"""cutroom: command-line entry point."""

from __future__ import annotations

import glob
import webbrowser
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

import typer

from . import obs
from .config import settings
from .obs import console

app = typer.Typer(add_completion=False, no_args_is_help=True,
                  help="Cutroom: an AI post-production team. Raw clips + a brief -> an edited, captioned, checked video.")


def _start(command: str) -> None:
    obs.setup(tags=[f"cmd:{command}", f"prompts:{settings.prompts_version}"])


@app.command()
def make(
    brief: str = typer.Argument(..., help="What you want, e.g. '30s vertical teaser for Instagram, energetic, captions'"),
    footage: list[str] = typer.Argument(..., help="Clip files or globs"),
    style: Optional[str] = typer.Option(None, help="Force a style profile (see styles/)"),
    music: Optional[Path] = typer.Option(None, help="Music track to mix under the edit (ducked under speech)"),
    project: Optional[str] = typer.Option(None, help="Project id (default: timestamp + brief)"),
    open_sheet: bool = typer.Option(False, "--open", help="Open the edit sheet when done"),
):
    """Edit raw footage into a finished short video from a one-line brief."""
    from .pipeline import project_dir, run_project

    files = [f for pattern in footage for f in (glob.glob(pattern) or [pattern]) if Path(f).is_file()]
    if not files:
        raise typer.BadParameter("no footage files found")
    _start("make")
    st = run_project(brief, files, project, style, str(music) if music else None)
    _done(st, project_dir(st.project_id), open_sheet)


@app.command()
def resume(project: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Project id under projects/")):
    """Continue an interrupted project from its last saved phase / editor step."""
    from .pipeline import project_dir, run_project
    from .models import ProjectState

    path = project_dir(project) / "state.json"
    st = ProjectState.model_validate_json(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    _start("resume")
    st = run_project(st.brief, st.footage, project)
    _done(st, project_dir(project), False)


def _done(st, folder: Path, open_sheet: bool) -> None:
    if st.phase == "done":
        console.rule(f"[green]done[/green] · {folder}")
        for k, v in st.outputs.items():
            console.print(f"  {k}: {folder / v}")
        if open_sheet:
            webbrowser.open((folder / st.outputs.get("sheet", "index.html")).resolve().as_uri())
    else:
        console.print(f"[red]stopped at {st.phase}[/red]: {st.error}\nResume with: cutroom resume {st.project_id}")


style_app = typer.Typer(help="Style profiles: the measurable editing style the editor follows.")
app.add_typer(style_app, name="style")


@style_app.command("learn")
def style_learn(
    refs: Optional[list[str]] = typer.Argument(None, help="Local reference videos you have the right to analyse"),
    url: Optional[list[str]] = typer.Option(None, "--url", help="Public YouTube video to learn from (watched, never downloaded)"),
    name: str = typer.Option(..., "--name", help="Name for the new style profile"),
):
    """Learn an editing style from references and save it as styles/<name>.json."""
    _start("style-learn")
    if url:
        from .references import learn as learn_urls

        profile = learn_urls(list(url), name)
    else:
        from .style import learn

        files = [Path(f) for p in (refs or []) for f in (glob.glob(p) or [p]) if Path(f).is_file()]
        if not files:
            raise typer.BadParameter("give local reference videos or --url links")
        profile = learn(files, name, settings.cache_dir / "style" / name)
    console.print_json(data={k: v for k, v in profile.items() if k not in ("learned_from", "measured_from")})


@style_app.command("list")
def style_list():
    """Show the available style profiles."""
    import json

    for p in sorted(settings.styles_dir.glob("*.json")):
        s = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        console.print(f"[bold]{p.stem}[/bold]: avg shot {s.get('avg_shot_seconds')}s · {s.get('description', '')[:110]}")


@app.command()
def studio(port: int = typer.Option(8765, help="Port for the studio UI"),
           open_browser: bool = typer.Option(True, "--open/--no-open", help="Open the studio in the browser")):
    """Open Cutroom Studio: the agentic editor UI (upload footage, pick a skill, watch the line edit it)."""
    import uvicorn

    _start("studio")
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    console.print(f"[bold]Cutroom Studio[/bold] → {url}")
    if open_browser:
        import threading

        threading.Timer(1.2, lambda: webbrowser.open(url)).start()
    uvicorn.run("cutroom.studio.server:app", host="127.0.0.1", port=port, log_level="warning")


@app.command()
def edit(
    footage: list[str] = typer.Argument(..., help="Raw clips (files or globs)"),
    skill: str = typer.Option("bonzo", help="Creative skill: bonzo, confessional, roaming, trailer, beatcut, super8, dreamy, clean"),
    aspect: str = typer.Option("9:16", help="9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5 or 2.39:1"),
    length: Optional[float] = typer.Option(None, help="Target seconds (default: decided from the footage)"),
    resolution: int = typer.Option(1080, help="Short side in pixels"),
    title: str = typer.Option("", help="Opening title"),
    stamp: str = typer.Option("", help="Time / place stamp, e.g. '7:28pm.'"),
    line: Optional[list[str]] = typer.Option(None, "--line", help="A story line (repeat for more)"),
    end: str = typer.Option("", help="End card text"),
    music: Optional[str] = typer.Option(None, help="'none', a file in music/, or a path to your own track"),
    reference: Optional[Path] = typer.Option(None, help="A reference video to edit like"),
    name: str = typer.Option("edit", help="Project name"),
):
    """Edit footage with the studio's agent line, headless (same agents as the UI)."""
    import shutil

    from .studio import line as ln
    from .studio.model import Clip, Reference, Settings, Track
    from .studio.skills import MUSIC_DIR

    files = [Path(f) for pattern in footage for f in (glob.glob(pattern) or [pattern]) if Path(f).is_file()]
    if not files:
        raise typer.BadParameter("no footage files found")
    _start("edit")
    p = ln.new_project(name)
    root = ln.project_dir(p.id)
    for i, f in enumerate(files, 1):
        dst = root / "media" / f"c{i}{f.suffix.lower()}"
        shutil.copyfile(f, dst)
        p.clips.append(Clip(id=f"c{i}", name=f.name, path=f"media/{dst.name}"))
    st = Settings(skill=skill, aspect=aspect, length=length, resolution=resolution, title=title, stamp=stamp,
                  story=list(line or []), end_card=end)
    if music:
        if music == "none":
            st.music = "none"
        elif (MUSIC_DIR / music).exists():
            st.music = f"library:{music}"
        elif Path(music).is_file():
            dst = root / "media" / f"music{Path(music).suffix.lower()}"
            shutil.copyfile(music, dst)
            p.music_upload = Track(name=Path(music).stem, path=f"media/{dst.name}", credit=Path(music).stem)
            st.music = "upload"
    if reference:
        dst = root / "media" / f"reference{reference.suffix.lower()}"
        shutil.copyfile(reference, dst)
        p.reference = Reference(name=reference.name, path=f"media/{dst.name}")
    p.settings = st
    p = ln.Line(p).run()
    console.rule(f"[{'green' if p.state == 'done' else 'red'}]{p.state}[/] · {root}")
    for k, a in p.agents.items():
        console.print(f"  {k:<12} {a.status:<8} {a.seconds:>6.1f}s  {a.summary}")
    if p.outputs.get("video"):
        console.print(f"\n  video: {root / p.outputs['video']}")


@app.command()
def doctor():
    """Check FFmpeg, the browser for graphics, and every model key."""
    import shutil

    from . import graphics, llm

    _start("doctor")
    for b in ("ffmpeg", "ffprobe"):
        console.print(f"{b}: {'[green]ok[/green]' if shutil.which(b) else '[red]missing[/red]'}")
    console.print(f"browser for graphics: {graphics.browser() or '[red]missing[/red]'}")
    console.print(f"GEMINI_API_KEY (vision): {'[green]set[/green]' if settings.gemini_api_key else '[red]missing[/red]'}")
    console.print(f"GROQ_API_KEY (speech-to-text): {'[green]set[/green]' if settings.groq_api_key else '[red]missing[/red]'}")
    for role in ("smart", "fast", "agent"):
        console.print(f"{role}: {', '.join(m for m in llm._chain(role))}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()

input.content:
# Cutroom Studio

**A video editor run by a crew of agents.** Drop raw footage, pick a creative skill (or give it a reference video
to edit like), write the story, and press *Run the line*. Eleven agents, each with one job, hand the edit down an
assembly line: measure the footage, grade it, cut it on the beat, reframe it, move it, set the type, mix the sound,
render it, and check the result.

There is **no model in the edit path**. Every decision is computed from measurements of your footage (FFmpeg decodes,
numpy measures), so the same footage and the same choices always give the same edit, it costs nothing to run, and
every agent can check its own work and say why it did what it did.

![Cutroom Studio](docs/studio.png)

```
uv sync
uv run cutroom studio            # opens http://127.0.0.1:8765
```

Needs FFmpeg 6+ with libass on PATH (`winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` / `brew install ffmpeg` / `apt install ffmpeg`).

> Built for #neatHack 2026: "Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching".

## The line

```
 Intake ─────┐
 Reference ──┼──▶ Colorist ────────────────────────────────┐
 Music ──────┘    Cutter ──▶ Reframer ──▶ Motion ──┬──▶ Typographer ──┬──▶ Export ──▶ QA
                                                   └──▶ Mixer ────────┘        │
                    ▲                                                          │
                    └────────── a failed check goes back to its owner ◀────────┘
```

Agents in the same column work at the same time. An agent whose inputs haven't changed since its last run is
**reused** instead of re-run: change a story line and only the Typographer, Export and QA run again (unchanged
segments aren't even re-rendered).

| Agent | Its one job | What it measures | How it checks itself |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Intake** | probes every clip, makes a light 1080p edit master (1 s keyframes) when the source is 4K or not H.264 | sharpness (Laplacian spread), motion, exposure, clipping, colour, camera cuts (adaptive histogram jumps), where the subject is, sound regions | every clip decodes and is measured end to end |
| **Reference** | watches your reference video *first* | shot-length distribution and bursts, CIELAB colour mean and spread, black/white points, grain, vignette, letterbox, dips to black, tempo and how often its cuts land on the beat | needs at least 3 shots to call it a rhythm |
| **Music** | picks the track and maps it | tempo (onset autocorrelation), beats (dynamic-programming beat tracker), downbeats (kick energy), energy per beat | a clear beat grid, or the cut falls back to the skill's own rhythm |
| **Colorist** | primary correction per clip, shot matching, then the skill's look or the reference's colour, baked into one 3D LUT per clip | levels, mid-grey, saturation and colour cast of each clip | no crushed blacks or blown highlights, a usable mid-grey; when a look crushes a clip it **trims exposure and contrast until its own checks pass**; ΔE to the reference |
| **Cutter** | plans the rhythm and picks a moment for every slot | interest per 0.1 s: sharpness, action, exposure, a clear subject | no cut crosses a camera cut; every cut on a beat when there is music |
| **Reframer** | fits each shot to your format | the subject's position over the shot | subject inside the middle 70% of the frame |
| **Motion** | the skill's moves | which shots hold still, which share a take, the source frame rate, footage beyond each cut | refuses slow motion the frame rate can't make smooth and transitions with no footage beyond the cut |
| **Typographer** | title, time/place stamp, story lines, end card | the graded brightness behind every line | every line placed with time to read it; a soft shade behind any line on a bright background |
| **Mixer** | music from a chosen downbeat, the footage's sound under it, ducking, fades | loudness (EBU R128, two passes) | −14 LUFS ±1, true peak under −1 dBTP |
| **Export** | renders segments in parallel, assembles cuts and transitions, burns in the type | | |
| **QA** | measures the finished file | duration, format, unintended black or frozen frames, loudness, pacing, cuts on the beat, colour distance from the reference | each failure names its owner and a fix; the line re-runs from that agent (up to two rounds) |

### How the cut is made (no model)

1. **Rhythm.** The skill gives a hold length and bursts of quick cuts (bonzo: ~2.2 s holds, a burst of four one-beat
   cuts every two holds). With music, holds snap to whole beats, bursts to beats or half beats, a burst waits until the
   music is loud enough, and the track is entered on the downbeat whose following stretch is loudest.
2. **Moments.** A dynamic program picks one window of footage per slot, maximising the window's score for its role
   (hook: action + sharpness, burst: action, hold: steady interest, outro: calm), in story order, with a gap between
   moments, never across a camera cut.
3. **Moves.** Static holds get a slow push-in; consecutive moments from the same take alternate a punch-in so the jump
   reads as intended; whip pans in and out of bursts (directional blur + slide) where there is footage beyond the cut.

## Skills

A skill is a recipe the agents execute: pacing, colour, moves, type and sound. Pick one, then tune it (pacing, look
strength, grain, music and footage levels, beat sync, transitions, slow motion). The skill gallery shows **your own
footage** in every look.

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| **bonzo** (inspired by @Wordisbonz) | life as a short film: serif title card on black, lowercase time stamp, the story in bold lowercase lines, warm soft film colour with grain and halation, handheld holds broken by whip-pan bursts on the beat |
| **confessional** (inspired by @farzatv) | talk to camera with every pause cut out: jump cuts hidden by alternating punch-ins, natural colour, the voice alone |
| **roaming doc** (inspired by @mayv_music) | handheld documentary: lowercase place stamps, phrase-by-phrase lines, cool muted film colour, rapid hard cuts on the beat |
| **trailer** | 2.39:1 letterbox, teal and orange, slow push-ins, dips to black between acts, spaced capitals on black cards |
| **beat cut** | a cut on every beat or half beat, punch zooms, white flashes into bursts, big words that land on the beat |
| **super 8** | home movie: faded warm stock, heavy grain, gate weave, flicker, an 18 fps cadence, light flashes, a date stamp |
| **dreamy** | a soft memory: dissolves, glowing highlights, pastel colour, slow push-ins, slow motion where the frame rate allows |
| **clean** | balanced colour, unhurried cuts, sentence-case lower thirds |

Only the *style* of the reference creators is used; Cutroom never copies their footage, music or words. Your text is
yours.

### Edit like a reference video

Add a reference and the Reference agent measures it before anything else. With *Edit like the reference* on, its
measured rhythm replaces the skill's (median shot length, how often bursts of short shots happen), the Colorist moves
your footage's colour to the reference's (Reinhard et al.'s mean-and-spread transfer in CIELAB, at the strength you
choose, with grain matched to the reference's measured noise), and its vignette, letterbox and beat sync carry over.

# Cutroom Studio

**A video editor run by a crew of agents.** Drop raw footage, pick a creative skill (or give it a reference video
to edit like), write the story, and press *Run the line*. Eleven agents, each with one job, hand the edit down an
assembly line: measure the footage, grade it, cut it on the beat, reframe it, move it, set the type, mix the sound,
render it, and check the result.

There is **no model in the edit path**. Every decision is computed from measurements of your footage (FFmpeg decodes,
numpy measures), so the same footage and the same choices always give the same edit, it costs nothing to run, and
every agent can check its own work and say why it did what it did.

![Cutroom Studio](docs/studio.png)

```
uv sync
uv run cutroom studio            # opens http://127.0.0.1:8765
```

Needs FFmpeg 6+ with libass on PATH (`winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` / `brew install ffmpeg` / `apt install ffmpeg`).

> Built for #neatHack 2026: "Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching".

## The line

```
 Intake ─────┐
 Reference ──┼──▶ Colorist ────────────────────────────────┐
 Music ──────┘    Cutter ──▶ Reframer ──▶ Motion ──┬──▶ Typographer ──┬──▶ Export ──▶ QA
                                                   └──▶ Mixer ────────┘        │
                    ▲                                                          │
                    └────────── a failed check goes back to its owner ◀────────┘
```

Agents in the same column work at the same time. An agent whose inputs haven't changed since its last run is
**reused** instead of re-run: change a story line and only the Typographer, Export and QA run again (unchanged
segments aren't even re-rendered).

| Agent | Its one job | What it measures | How it checks itself |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Intake** | probes every clip, makes a light 1080p edit master (1 s keyframes) when the source is 4K or not H.264 | sharpness (Laplacian spread), motion, exposure, clipping, colour, camera cuts (adaptive histogram jumps), where the subject is, sound regions | every clip decodes and is measured end to end |
| **Reference** | watches your reference video *first* | shot-length distribution and bursts, CIELAB colour mean and spread, black/white points, grain, vignette, letterbox, dips to black, tempo and how often its cuts land on the beat | needs at least 3 shots to call it a rhythm |
| **Music** | picks the track and maps it | tempo (onset autocorrelation), beats (dynamic-programming beat tracker), downbeats (kick energy), energy per beat | a clear beat grid, or the cut falls back to the skill's own rhythm |
| **Colorist** | primary correction per clip, shot matching, then the skill's look or the reference's colour, baked into one 3D LUT per clip | levels, mid-grey, saturation and colour cast of each clip | no crushed blacks or blown highlights, a usable mid-grey; when a look crushes a clip it **trims exposure and contrast until its own checks pass**; ΔE to the reference |
| **Cutter** | plans the rhythm and picks a moment for every slot | interest per 0.1 s: sharpness, action, exposure, a clear subject | no cut crosses a camera cut; every cut on a beat when there is music |
| **Reframer** | fits each shot to your format | the subject's position over the shot | subject inside the middle 70% of the frame |
| **Motion** | the skill's moves | which shots hold still, which share a take, the source frame rate, footage beyond each cut | refuses slow motion the frame rate can't make smooth and transitions with no footage beyond the cut |
| **Typographer** | title, time/place stamp, story lines, end card | the graded brightness behind every line | every line placed with time to read it; a soft shade behind any line on a bright background |
| **Mixer** | music from a chosen downbeat, the footage's sound under it, ducking, fades | loudness (EBU R128, two passes) | −14 LUFS ±1, true peak under −1 dBTP |
| **Export** | renders segments in parallel, assembles cuts and transitions, burns in the type | | |
| **QA** | measures the finished file | duration, format, unintended black or frozen frames, loudness, pacing, cuts on the beat, colour distance from the reference | each failure names its owner and a fix; the line re-runs from that agent (up to two rounds) |

### How the cut is made (no model)

1. **Rhythm.** The skill gives a hold length and bursts of quick cuts (bonzo: ~2.2 s holds, a burst of four one-beat
   cuts every two holds). With music, holds snap to whole beats, bursts to beats or half beats, a burst waits until the
   music is loud enough, and the track is entered on the downbeat whose following stretch is loudest.
2. **Moments.** A dynamic program picks one window of footage per slot, maximising the window's score for its role
   (hook: action + sharpness, burst: action, hold: steady interest, outro: calm), in story order, with a gap between
   moments, never across a camera cut.
3. **Moves.** Static holds get a slow push-in; consecutive moments from the same take alternate a punch-in so the jump
   reads as intended; whip pans in and out of bursts (directional blur + slide) where there is footage beyond the cut.

A skill is a recipe the agents execute: pacing, colour, moves, type and sound. Pick one, then tune it (pacing, look
strength, grain, music and footage levels, beat sync, transitions, slow motion). The skill gallery shows **your own
footage** in every look.

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| **bonzo** (inspired by @Wordisbonz) | life as a short film: serif title card on black, lowercase time stamp, the story in bold lowercase lines, warm soft film colour with grain and halation, handheld holds broken by whip-pan bursts on the beat |
| **confessional** (inspired by @farzatv) | talk to camera with every pause cut out: jump cuts hidden by alternating punch-ins, natural colour, the voice alone |
| **roaming doc** (inspired by @mayv_music) | handheld documentary: lowercase place stamps, phrase-by-phrase lines, cool muted film colour, rapid hard cuts on the beat |
| **trailer** | 2.39:1 letterbox, teal and orange, slow push-ins, dips to black between acts, spaced capitals on black cards |
| **beat cut** | a cut on every beat or half beat, punch zooms, white flashes into bursts, big words that land on the beat |
| **super 8** | home movie: faded warm stock, heavy grain, gate weave, flicker, an 18 fps cadence, light flashes, a date stamp |
| **dreamy** | a soft memory: dissolves, glowing highlights, pastel colour, slow push-ins, slow motion where the frame rate allows |
| **clean** | balanced colour, unhurried cuts, sentence-case lower thirds |
