# Cutroom

**An AI post-production team you can hand raw footage and a one-line brief, and walk away.**
A logger watches every clip, a producer writes the spec, an editor agent cuts it with real editing tools, a motion
designer makes the titles and thumbnail, and a critic watches every draft and sends it back until it's good enough to
post. Every render is measured (length, black and frozen frames, loudness, pacing, caption speed), every decision is
traced in [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com), and a crash resumes mid-edit.

```
$ cutroom make "30s vertical teaser for Reels: open on the robot attack, best dialogue with captions, end on the title" \
    footage/tears-of-steel/*.mov
```

Outputs: `final.mp4` (9:16, word-by-word captions, animated titles, loudness-normalised to −14 LUFS), `thumbnail.png`,
`captions.srt`, and an **edit sheet** (`index.html`): the cut list with a frame per segment, every quality check, and
the creative director's notes, round by round.

> Built for #neatHack 2026 ("Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching"). Work in progress.

## The team

| Agent | What it decides | What keeps it honest |
|---|---|---|
| **Logger** | Watches each clip (Gemini video understanding on a 360p proxy) and logs it shot by shot: description, energy, quality, usefulness, highlights | Shot boundaries snapped to FFmpeg scene changes; words and timings come from Whisper, not from the model; if no vision model is available it logs from scene cuts + transcript and the edit continues |
| **Producer** | Platform, aspect ratio, target length, hook, structure, captions, titles, house style | Target length clamped to what the footage can actually fill |
| **Editor** (tool-calling loop) | Every cut: `list_shots`, `read_transcript`, `add_segment`, `trim_segment`, `move_segment`, `set_zoom`, `set_captions`, `add_title`, `preview`, `render_draft`, `finish` | Times must exist in the source; cuts that land mid-word are flagged with the nearest clean point; the running duration and pacing are shown after every action; `finish` is refused until the current timeline is rendered and its checks pass |
| **Motion designer** | Title cards, lower thirds, end cards, thumbnail | HTML/CSS templates rendered to transparent PNGs and animated by FFmpeg, in the house style |
| **Critic** | Watches the rendered draft like a creative director: hook, pacing, story, legibility, anything broken; approve or revise with up to 4 concrete fixes | Measurable checks run on every render; approval needs a score ≥ 7 |

## Taste without fine-tuning: learn a creator's style from their public videos

```
cutroom style learn --name bonzo --url https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sKdC4Bs-cKA --url https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tonG-OufefQ
```

A vision model watches windows of the creator's **public** videos through Gemini's own YouTube-URL input (nothing is
downloaded or re-used) and reports, in a fixed structure: the time of every cut, every piece of on-screen text (words,
case, position, size, font feel), the look (temperature, contrast, saturation, black level, grain, vignette,
letterbox), camera, transitions and speed changes, sound (voice-over vs to-camera, music role, cuts on the beat), how
the video opens and is built, and its signature moves. Cutroom turns that into a **style profile** the renderer can
execute and the critic can measure against: shot rhythm, a concrete grade, the text treatment, the story structure.

Profiles learned from the references this project was asked to edit like:

| Profile | Learned signature |
|---|---|
| `bonzo` (@Wordisbonz, "turning my life into short movies") | the story told in bold lowercase text lines; time/place stamps; long handheld walk-and-talk takes with occasional whip-pan bursts; warm, soft, lightly grained look; centred serif title cards on black |
| `farza` (@farzatv) | direct-to-camera confessional; tight jump cuts that remove every pause inside a take; handheld selfie framing that drifts to B-roll; no text, no music |
| `mayv` (@mayv_music) | handheld roaming documentary; location stamps; phrase-by-phrase lowercase subtitles; rapid hard cuts on the beat in music sections |

Only the style is learned. The editor writes its own lines about *your* footage; lines copied from the reference
creator are refused, and the raw observations (which quote the creators' on-screen text) stay out of the repo. Cut
timings come from a vision model sampling 3 frames a second, so rhythm is an estimate (two models disagreed by 3x on
one creator; the stronger model's reading is used).

For local reference videos you have the right to analyse, `cutroom style learn <files> --name x` measures them
directly with FFmpeg instead (shot-length distribution, brightness/saturation, loudness, words per second).

## What the editor can do

Cuts and trims, **jump cuts that strip pauses out of talking footage** (alternating a subtle punch-in to hide them),
slow motion and speed changes, dip-to-black, punch-in zooms, **subject-aware reframing** to vertical, word-by-word or
minimal lowercase captions, **story text and time/place stamps**, title and end cards, music ducked under speech, and a
**film look** per style (colour temperature, lifted or crushed blacks, vignette, grain, letterbox). Flat/log footage gets
an automatic **primary colour correction** (levels stretch, mid-tone and saturation recovery) before the creative look,
and anything over 1080p is edited from an optimised 1080p master.

## Demo footage

The demos use Blender Foundation open movies (*Tears of Steel*, *Sintel*), CC BY 3.0. See `footage/README.md`.

import sys
sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
import numpy as np
from cutroom.studio import line as ln, look, skills
from cutroom.studio.agents.base import Ctx
from cutroom.studio.agents.colorist import clip_pixels, self_correct
from cutroom.studio.agents.reference import analyse_reference, describe
pid = "20261011-191325-53fd"
p = ln.Project.model_validate_json((ln.project_dir(pid) / "project.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
root = ln.project_dir(pid)
ctx = Ctx(project=p, root=root, emit=lambda *a, **k: None)
prof = analyse_reference(ctx)
print("\n".join(describe(prof)))
ref = prof["look"]
pxs = [clip_pixels(ctx, c) for c in p.clips]
prims = [look.primary_params(x) for x in pxs]
src = look.stats(np.concatenate([look.apply_primary(x, pr) for x, pr in zip(pxs, prims)]))
sk = skills.with_reference(skills.get("trailer"), prof, 0.85)
lk, s = sk["look"], sk["look_strength_scale"]
match = {"src": src, "ref": ref, "strength": 0.85}

"""Observability: neatlogs tracing plus a human-readable event stream.

Every notable step goes three places: the terminal (for the operator / demo),
the run's events.jsonl (so a run can be audited after the fact), and neatlogs
(as a log span inside the active trace, so the Coach can find it later).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextvars
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import neatlogs
from rich.console import Console

from .config import settings

console = Console(highlight=False)

_initialized = False
_sink: contextvars.ContextVar[Path | None] = contextvars.ContextVar("uw_event_sink", default=None)
_counters: contextvars.ContextVar[dict | None] = contextvars.ContextVar("uw_counters", default=None)

STYLE = {
    "plan": "cyan",
    "produce": "cyan",
    "log": "magenta",
    "edit": "bold cyan",
    "render": "blue",
    "qa": "green",
    "critic": "bold magenta",
    "design": "yellow",
    "style": "bold yellow",
    "crust": "magenta",
    "web": "blue",
    "extract": "white",
    "verify": "green",
    "conflict": "bold yellow",
    "recover": "bold yellow",
    "inject": "red",
    "fail": "bold red",
    "memo": "bold green",
    "coach": "bold cyan",
    "agent": "bold cyan",
    "skeptic": "bold magenta",
    "watch": "bold red",
    "eval": "bold white",
    "info": "dim",
}


def setup(tags: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    """Initialise neatlogs once per process. Safe to call when no key is set (spans just aren't exported)."""
    global _initialized
    if _initialized:
        return
    neatlogs.init(
        api_key=settings.neatlogs_api_key or None,
        workflow_name="cutroom",
        instrumentations=["openai", "google_genai"],
        tags=["cutroom", *(tags or [])],
    )
    _initialized = True


def bind_run(events_path: Path) -> tuple[contextvars.Token, contextvars.Token]:
    events_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return _sink.set(events_path), _counters.set({})


def unbind_run(tokens: tuple[contextvars.Token, contextvars.Token]) -> None:
    _sink.reset(tokens[0])
    _counters.reset(tokens[1])


def counters() -> dict:
    return dict(_counters.get() or {})


def emit(kind: str, msg: str, **data: Any) -> None:
    """Record one event. `kind` is a short tag like 'crust', 'recover', 'verify'."""
    style = STYLE.get(kind, "white")
    console.print(f"[{style}]\\[{kind:<8}][/{style}] {msg}")

    c = _counters.get()
    if c is not None:
        c[kind] = c.get(kind, 0) + 1

    sink = _sink.get()
    if sink is not None:
        with sink.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps({"t": time.time(), "kind": kind, "msg": msg, **data}, default=str) + "\n")

    if kind in ("recover", "inject", "fail", "conflict"):
        neatlogs.log(
            "{kind}: {msg}",
            level="warning" if kind != "fail" else "error",
            kind=kind,
            msg=msg,
            **{k: v for k, v in data.items() if isinstance(v, (str, int, float, bool))},
        )


def current_trace_id() -> str | None:
    """The OpenTelemetry trace id of the active span, as neatlogs shows it."""
    try:
        from opentelemetry import trace

        ctx = trace.get_current_span().get_span_context()
        return format(ctx.trace_id, "032x") if ctx and ctx.trace_id else None
    except Exception:
        return None


def set_attrs(**attrs: Any) -> None:
    """Attach attributes (e.g. final metrics) to the active neatlogs span."""
    try:
        from opentelemetry import trace

        span = trace.get_current_span()
        for k, v in attrs.items():
            if isinstance(v, (str, int, float, bool)):
                span.set_attribute(f"cutroom.{k}", v)
    except Exception:
        pass

"""QA: measures the finished video and sends failures back to the agent responsible.

Every check is a measurement of the rendered file (or the edit that made it): duration, format, black and
frozen frames that weren't intended, loudness and true peak, pacing against the skill, cuts on the beat,
colour distance from the reference. A failure names its owner and a fix; the line re-runs from that agent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from ... import media
from .. import analysis as an
from .. import look
from ..model import AgentRun
from .base import Agent, Ctx, frame_size, out_fps


class QA(Agent):
    key, title, icon, color = "qa", "QA", "shield", "#41a6b5"
    role = "measures the finished video and sends any failure back to the agent responsible"
    needs = ("export",)

    def inputs(self, ctx: Ctx):
        return [ctx.project.outputs.get("bytes"), ctx.project.outputs.get("duration")]

    def run(self, ctx: Ctx, rep: AgentRun) -> None:
        p, s = ctx.project, ctx.settings
        final = ctx.root / "final.mp4"
        info = media.probe(final)
        W, H = frame_size(s)
        fps = out_fps(p)
        T = p.duration
        self.check(ctx, rep, "render complete", abs(info["duration"] - T) <= 2.5 / fps + 0.05 and info["has_audio"],
                   f"{info['duration']:.2f}s vs {T:.2f}s planned, audio {'yes' if info['has_audio'] else 'missing'}",
                   owner="export")
        self.check(ctx, rep, "format", (info["width"], info["height"]) == (W, H), f"{info['width']}x{info['height']}",
                   owner="export")
        if s.length:
            self.check(ctx, rep, "length", abs(T - s.length) <= max(1.0, 0.06 * s.length),
                       f"{T:.1f}s for a {s.length:.0f}s target", owner="cutter",
                       hint={"length_scale": round(s.length / max(T, 0.1), 3)})
        # intended black: cards and fades
        planned = [(g.start, g.start + g.length) for g in p.timeline if g.kind == "card"]
        planned += [(g.start, g.start + g.fade_in + 0.15) for g in p.timeline if g.fade_in]
        planned += [(g.start + g.length - g.fade_out - 0.15, g.start + g.length) for g in p.timeline if g.fade_out]

        def intended(a: float, b: float) -> bool:
            return any(a >= x - 0.12 and b <= y + 0.12 for x, y in planned)

        blacks = [(a, b) for a, b in media.black_frames(final, 0.25) if not intended(a, b)]
        avoid = []
        for a, b in blacks:
            for g in p.timeline:
                if g.kind == "clip" and g.start < b and a < g.start + g.length:
                    sa = g.src_in + max(a - g.start, 0) * g.speed
                    avoid.append([g.clip, round(sa, 2), round(sa + (b - a) * g.speed, 2)])
        self.check(ctx, rep, "no unintended black", not blacks,
                   "none" if not blacks else ", ".join(f"{a:.1f}–{b:.1f}s" for a, b in blacks[:3]),
                   owner="cutter", hint={"avoid": avoid})
        frozen = [t for t in media.frozen_frames(final, 1.2)
                  if not any(x - 0.1 <= t <= y for x, y in planned)]
        self.check(ctx, rep, "no frozen picture", not frozen, "none" if not frozen else ", ".join(f"{t:.1f}s" for t in frozen[:3]),
                   owner="cutter", hint={"length_scale": 0.92})
        loud = media.loudness(final)
        if loud:
            self.check(ctx, rep, "loudness", abs(loud["lufs"] - p.audio.lufs) <= 1.2 and loud["true_peak"] <= -0.3,
                       f"{loud['lufs']:.1f} LUFS (target {p.audio.lufs:g}), peak {loud['true_peak']:.1f} dBTP", owner="mixer")
        clips = [g for g in p.timeline if g.kind == "clip"]
        P = ctx.skill.get("pace") or {}
        if clips and not P.get("jumpcut"):
            holds = [g.length for g in clips if g.role != "burst"]
            target = float(P.get("shot", 2.5)) / max(s.pacing, 0.3)
            avg = float(np.mean(holds)) if holds else 0
            ok = 0.55 * target <= avg <= 1.8 * target
            self.check(ctx, rep, "pacing", ok, f"average hold {avg:.2f}s vs {target:.2f}s for {ctx.skill.get('label')}",
                       owner="cutter")
        if p.track and s.beat_sync and len(p.track.beats) > 8 and clips:
            bt = np.array(p.track.beats) - p.audio.music_in
            sub = np.sort(np.concatenate([bt, (bt[:-1] + bt[1:]) / 2]))
            cut_pts = [g.start + (g.trans_d / 2 if g.trans != "cut" else 0) for g in clips[1:]]
            on = sum(1 for c in cut_pts if np.min(np.abs(sub - c)) <= 1.0 / fps + 0.005)
            self.check(ctx, rep, "cuts on the beat", not cut_pts or on >= 0.85 * len(cut_pts),
                       f"{on}/{len(cut_pts)} cuts within a frame of a beat", owner="cutter")
        ref = p.reference
        if ref and ref.profile and s.match_reference and clips:
            fr = an.frames(final, 2.0, an.analysis_size(W, H, 160))
            keep = [i for i in range(len(fr)) if not any(x <= i / 2.0 <= y for x, y in planned)]
            if keep:
                px = look.pixel_sample(fr[keep])

Your usage limit has been reached, so I'm stopping here. (The "failed" notice just above is only the old server instance I shut down; the new one is running.)

I scrapped the reel maker and built **Cutroom Studio**: a video editor run by 11 agents, with no AI model making edit decisions. It's running at **http://127.0.0.1:8765**.

**How it works**
- **Your flow:** drop in raw footage, pick a skill, choose the format, write your title, time stamp and story lines, then press *Run the line*. You can add a reference video and it gets measured first, then your footage is edited to match its rhythm, colour, grain and letterbox.
- **The agents:** intake, reference, music, colorist, cutter, reframer, motion, typographer, mixer, export, QA. Each has one job and checks its own work. Agents that don't depend on each other run at the same time. QA measures the finished video and sends any failure back to the agent responsible.
- **Speed on re-runs:** an agent whose inputs didn't change is reused, so editing a story line only re-runs the type, export and QA.
- **Skills:** bonzo (life as a short film), confessional, roaming doc, trailer, beat cut, super 8, dreamy, clean. The skill gallery shows your own footage in each look.
- **The UI:** media bin, viewer with a before/after colour slider, the live assembly line (click any agent to see its decisions and checks), a timeline with beats and transitions, and a report with downloads (MP4, plus an edit list that opens in Premiere or Resolve).

**Tested**
- Your rocks clip, bonzo skill: serif title card on black, lowercase story text, warm film colour fixed from the flat grey original, all 7 cuts on the beat, every QA check passes.
- Trailer cut from Tears of Steel to match the Sintel trailer as a reference: delivered, but QA flagged two bugs (beat drift and the end-card black check). Both are fixed and committed; this edit hasn't been re-run with the fixes yet.
- Beat cut: all QA checks pass.
- 9 offline tests of the core algorithms pass.

content.text:
**What problem Underwrite solves**

Before an investor puts money into a startup, someone has to answer basic questions:

- Is this company real?
- How much has it raised?
- Who are the founders?
- Is the team growing or shrinking?
- What's in the news?

That research usually takes an analyst **2–4 hours of Googling per company**, and they do it for dozens of companies a week.

Underwrite does it in about **5 minutes** and writes it up as a one-page memo, like the Sequoia memo you showed me.

**Why someone would use it instead of ChatGPT:** ChatGPT can confidently make up numbers. Underwrite checks every fact against a real source and links it. If it can't verify something, it says so. If two sources disagree (the company says 200 employees, the data says 80), it shows you the conflict instead of hiding it. It can also re-check companies every night and tell you when something changes. That's the hackathon theme: an agent you trust without watching.

**Who would use it:**
- Angel investors and VC analysts, before a meeting with a startup.
- Sales teams researching a company before a call.
- Job seekers checking whether a startup is solid before joining.

**Honest weak spots:**
- Paid tools like Crunchbase or Tracxn already give investors raw data. Underwrite's edge is the verified, written memo, not the data itself.
- Investors are a narrow audience, and it's harder for you to demo something you don't personally feel the pain of.

**My suggestion:** the scam-checker idea is basically Underwrite pointed at a problem you and every student know: *"Is this company and this offer real?"* About 70% of the engine is already built (company lookup, web search, fact checking, sources). Reframing it around job and internship offers gives you something you understand and can demo with feeling, and it can realistically be done in the 28 hours left.

Which way do you want to go?
1. **Keep Underwrite as it is** and spend the time on the demo video and posts.
2. **Build the offer scam checker** in a new folder, reusing Underwrite's engine.

content.text:
Yes, there are competitors, and the space is crowded. Here's the honest picture (from what I know as of mid-2026; I haven't searched live):

**Direct competitors (AI research or due-diligence reports on companies)**
| Who | What they do | Price / who for |
|---|---|---|
| **Wokelo** | AI-written due-diligence and company-research reports | Enterprise, sold to PE/VC firms and consultancies |
| **Hebbia** | AI that reads huge piles of documents for finance teams | Enterprise, big funds and banks |
| **Rogo**, **Brightwave** | "AI analyst" for investors: research and summaries | Enterprise finance teams |
| **AlphaSense** | Market intelligence with AI search over filings, news and expert calls | Expensive, big firms |

**Generic deep-research tools anyone can use**
- ChatGPT Deep Research, Perplexity, Gemini Deep Research. Type a company name and you get a long report.

**Data platforms (raw data, not memos)**
- Crunchbase, PitchBook, Tracxn, CB Insights, Harmonic. They give the numbers; you still write the memo yourself.

**Where Underwrite is different**
1. **It checks every fact.** Each line in the memo is verified against a source. Deep Research tools write fluent reports but can still slip in made-up numbers.
2. **It shows conflicts.** When sources disagree, it tells you instead of picking one quietly.
3. **It keeps watching.** It re-checks companies every night and alerts you only when something actually changed.
4. **It's free and open.** The others cost thousands of dollars a year per seat.
5. **You can see why it said what it said.** Every step is traced in neatlogs.

**Does it matter for the hackathon?** Not much. Judges score the agent (30%), tool use (25%), demo (20%), building in public (15%) and originality (10%). Having competitors only touches originality. And "Deep Research makes things up, Underwrite proves every line" is a strong pitch for the theme "agents you'd trust to run without you watching."

**My recommendation:** keep Underwrite. It's built, tested, fits the theme, and the competitors make the story easy to tell. Use the remaining ~28 hours on:
1. Finishing the before/after numbers (the eval that's paused).
2. Recording a sharp demo video.
3. Posting the #neatHack updates.
4. Getting the cfo.ai business plan done.

Want me to start on that?

# neatHack 2026 — Underwrite

## Project

**Underwrite** — an autonomous due-diligence agent you can leave running overnight.
Give it a list of startups; it plans the research, pulls company data from Crustdata,
searches and reads the web, extracts every factual claim with a source, has an
independent verifier check each claim against the source text, flags contradictions
(e.g. "website says 50 people, Crustdata says 18"), and writes a cited investment memo
as a three-page paper dossier (HTML, PDF, PNG).

A **Coach** loop reads the agent's own neatlogs traces, detections and triage fixes
over the neatlogs MCP server, rewrites the agent's prompts, re-runs the eval set,
and only keeps a change if the numbers improve.

def coach(base: str, run_eval: bool = True, split: str = "all") -> dict:
    mode = settings.mode
    eval_path = evals.latest_eval(base, mode)
    if eval_path is None:
        emit("coach", f"no {mode} eval found for {base}; running one first")
        eval_path = evals.run_eval(base, split, mode=mode)
    emit("coach", f"baseline: {eval_path.parent.name}")

    failures, worst_traces = local_failures(eval_path)
    emit("coach", f"local evidence: {len(failures['wrong_facts'])} wrong facts, {len(failures['rejected_claims'])} "
                  f"rejected claims, {len(failures['unanswered_questions'])} unanswered questions")
    from_neatlogs = ask_neatlogs(worst_traces)

    base_dir = settings.prompts_dir / base
    used = AGENT_PROMPTS if mode == "agent" else PIPELINE_PROMPTS
    current = {p.stem: p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for p in sorted(base_dir.glob("*.md")) if p.stem in used}
    files_text = "\n\n".join(f"=== {name}.md ===\n{text}" for name, text in current.items())

    out = _propose(AGENT if mode == "agent" else PIPELINE, files_text, failures, from_neatlogs)

    accepted_files: dict[str, str] = {}
    for name, text in out.files.items():
        name = name.removesuffix(".md")
        if name not in current:
            emit("coach", f"ignoring proposed file '{name}' (not a known prompt)")
        elif prompts.SPLIT not in text:
            emit("coach", f"rejecting {name}: missing {prompts.SPLIT}")
        elif _placeholders(text) != _placeholders(current[name]):
            emit("coach", f"rejecting {name}: placeholders changed {_placeholders(current[name])} -> {_placeholders(text)}")
        elif text.strip() != current[name].strip():
            accepted_files[name] = text.strip() + "\n"
    if not accepted_files:
        emit("coach", "no valid prompt changes proposed; nothing to evaluate")
        return {"base": base, "new": None, "decision": "no-change", "diagnosis": out.diagnosis}

    new = next_version()
    new_dir = settings.prompts_dir / new
    shutil.copytree(base_dir, new_dir)
    for leftover in ("COACH_NOTES.md", "coach_report.json"):
        (new_dir / leftover).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    for name, text in accepted_files.items():
        (new_dir / f"{name}.md").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    emit("coach", f"wrote prompts/{new}: changed {', '.join(sorted(accepted_files))}")

    report = {
        "base": base,
        "new": new,
        "baseline_eval": str(eval_path.relative_to(settings.runs_dir)),
        "neatlogs_sources": sorted(from_neatlogs),
        "diagnosis": out.diagnosis,
        "changes": [c.model_dump() for c in out.changes if c.prompt.removesuffix(".md") in accepted_files],
        "decision": "pending-eval",
    }
    if run_eval:
        new_eval = evals.run_eval(new, split, mode=mode)
        report["new_eval"] = str(new_eval.relative_to(settings.runs_dir))
        report["train"] = evals.compare(eval_path, new_eval, "train")
        report["test"] = evals.compare(eval_path, new_eval, "test")
        report["decision"] = decide(report["train"])
        emit("coach", f"decision: {report['decision']} prompts {new}")
    _write_notes(new_dir, report)
    return report


def decide(train: dict) -> str:
    """Keep the new version only if it is better on what it was optimised for, at a sane cost."""
    def d(k: str) -> float:
        return train.get(k, {}).get("delta", 0)

    quality = d("fact_accuracy") + d("supported_rate") + d("coverage") + 0.5 * d("fact_precision")
    cost_before = train.get("usd_per_memo", {}).get("before", 0) or 1e-9
    cost_ok = d("usd_per_memo") / cost_before < 0.5
    return "accepted" if quality > 0 and cost_ok else "rejected"


def _propose(design: str, files_text: str, failures: dict, neat: dict) -> CoachOut:
    system = (
        "You are an expert AI agent engineer. You improve a due-diligence research agent by rewriting its prompt "
        "files. Base every change on the evidence given (eval failures and neatlogs traces/detections/triage) and "
        "cite that evidence. Keep every {{placeholder}} exactly as it is and keep the ---USER--- separator. Prefer a "
        "few targeted, high-leverage edits over rewriting everything. Never add facts about specific companies to "
        "the prompts (that would overfit the eval). Respond with only a JSON object."
    )
    neat_text = "\n\n".join(f"--- {k} ---\n{v}" for k, v in neat.items()) or "(neatlogs MCP was not reachable)"
    user = (
        f"{design}\n\nCURRENT PROMPT FILES:\n{files_text}\n\n"
        f"EVAL FAILURES (train split):\n{json.dumps(failures, indent=2)[:30000]}\n\n"
        f"NEATLOGS (via MCP):\n{neat_text[:30000]}\n\n"
        'Return JSON: {"diagnosis": ["root cause 1", ...], "changes": [{"prompt": "extractor", "why": "...", '
        '"evidence": "which failures / trace / detection this addresses"}], "files": {"extractor": "<complete new '
        'file content, including ---USER--->"}}. Include in "files" only the prompts you changed.'
    )
    with neatlogs.trace("prompt.coach", kind="CHAIN", version="coach-1"):
        text, model = llm.complete("smart", system, user, effort="high", max_tokens=32000)
    try:
        return CoachOut.model_validate(llm._extract_json(text))
    except Exception as e:
        emit("recover", f"coach output was not valid JSON ({str(e)[:80]}); asking for a repair")
        fixed, _ = llm.complete("fast", "Fix this into valid JSON matching the requested shape. Output only JSON.",
                                f"Schema: {json.dumps(CoachOut.model_json_schema())}\n\nOutput:\n{text}", max_tokens=32000)
        return CoachOut.model_validate(llm._extract_json(fixed))


def _write_notes(new_dir: Path, report: dict) -> None:
    lines = [f"# Coach notes: {report['base']} -> {report['new']}", "",
             f"Decision: **{report['decision']}**  ", f"Baseline eval: `{report['baseline_eval']}`  ",
             f"neatlogs evidence used: {', '.join(report['neatlogs_sources']) or 'none (MCP unreachable)'}", "",
             "## Diagnosis", *[f"- {d}" for d in report["diagnosis"]], "", "## Changes"]
    for c in report["changes"]:
        lines += [f"### {c['prompt']}", c["why"], "", f"_Evidence:_ {c['evidence']}", ""]
    for split in ("train", "test"):
        if split in report:
            lines += [f"## Result ({split} split)", "", "| metric | before | after | change |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
            lines += [f"| {k} | {v['before']:g} | {v['after']:g} | {v['delta']:+.3g} |" for k, v in report[split].items()]
            lines.append("")
    (new_dir / "COACH_NOTES.md").write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
    (new_dir / "coach_report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    console.print(f"[bold]Coach notes:[/bold] {new_dir / 'COACH_NOTES.md'}")

1	# Underwrite: business plan (inputs for cfo.ai)
2	
3	This is the plan we model in cfo.ai. Numbers marked **measured** come from real runs (`runs/*/state.json`,
4	`runs/eval-*/eval.json`). Numbers marked **assumption** are ours to defend and are the levers to play with in cfo.ai.
5	
6	## The product
7	
8	A due-diligence analyst that runs unattended: a watchlist of startups goes in, cited and verified first-pass memos
9	come out every morning, as a web page and a PDF dossier. Buyers: angel investors, micro-VCs and seed funds, accelerator
10	selection teams, and corp-dev / M&A teams screening targets.
11	
12	**Why they pay:** a first-pass memo costs an analyst 2–4 hours (at $60–120/hour fully loaded that is $120–480 per
13	company). Underwrite produces one in about 4 minutes, with every fact sourced and checked, for well under $1 of cost.
14	
15	## Unit economics per memo
16	
17	| Item | Value | Source |
18	|---|---|---|
19	| Crustdata credits per memo | ~18 | **measured** (company record 2, ~10 searches, ~8 page fetches, minus cache hits) |
20	| Price per Crustdata credit | $0.02 | **assumption**: Crustdata doesn't publish a self-serve rate; replace with the rate on your plan |
21	| Data cost per memo | ~$0.36 | 18 × $0.02 |
22	| LLM tokens per memo | ~20–25k | **measured** (neatlogs trace totals, e.g. 21,602 tokens for Razorpay) |
23	| LLM cost per memo (paid list price) | ~$0.013 | **measured** at Gemini paid-tier list prices; $0 on free tiers |
24	| Compute per memo | ~$0.002 | t3.small at $0.0208/h, ~4 min per memo |
25	| **Total cost per memo** | **~$0.38** | |
26	| Time per memo | 3–5 min | **measured** |
27	
28	## Pricing (assumption)
29	
30	| Plan | Price | Includes | Cost to serve | Gross margin |
31	|---|---|---|---|---|
32	| Angel | $49 / month | 25 memos, PDF export | 25 × $0.38 = $9.50 | ~81% |
33	| Fund | $399 / month | 300 memos, nightly watchlist, 5 seats, Slack digest | 300 × $0.38 = $114 | ~71% |
34	| Enterprise | from $2,000 / month | custom sources, private deployment, SSO, SLA | ~$500 | ~75% |
35	| Overage | $1.50 / memo | | $0.38 | ~75% |
36	
37	## Fixed monthly costs (assumption)
38	
39	| Item | Month 1–6 | Month 7–12 |
40	|---|---|---|
41	| Hosting (EC2 + storage + backups) | $60 | $250 |
42	| Tooling (neatlogs Pro, GitHub, email, domain) | $150 | $300 |
43	| Founder salary | $0 (bootstrapped) | $4,000 |
44	| First hire (engineer, from month 7) | – | $6,000 |
45	| Marketing | $300 | $1,500 |
46	| **Total** | **~$510** | **~$12,050** |
47	
48	## Revenue scenario (assumption, to stress-test in cfo.ai)
49	
50	| Month | Angel | Fund | Enterprise | MRR |
51	|---|---|---|---|---|
52	| 1 | 5 | 0 | 0 | $245 |
53	| 3 | 25 | 3 | 0 | $2,422 |
54	| 6 | 60 | 10 | 1 | $8,930 |
55	| 9 | 110 | 22 | 2 | $18,168 |
56	| 12 | 160 | 35 | 4 | $29,805 |
57	
58	Starting cash: $5,000 (founder) + $10,000 assumed pre-seed/grant in month 6.
59	
60	## Questions to ask Ari (cfo.ai)
61	
62	Paste these after entering the numbers above:
63	
64	1. "Build a 12-month model from these plans, costs and the revenue scenario. Show MRR, gross margin, burn and ending cash per month."

# Underwrite: business plan (inputs for cfo.ai)

This is the plan we model in cfo.ai. Numbers marked **measured** come from real runs (`runs/*/state.json`,
`runs/eval-*/eval.json`). Numbers marked **assumption** are ours to defend and are the levers to play with in cfo.ai.

## The product

A due-diligence analyst that runs unattended: a watchlist of startups goes in, cited and verified first-pass memos
come out every morning, as a web page and a PDF dossier. Buyers: angel investors, micro-VCs and seed funds, accelerator
selection teams, and corp-dev / M&A teams screening targets.

**Why they pay:** a first-pass memo costs an analyst 2–4 hours (at $60–120/hour fully loaded that is $120–480 per
company). Underwrite produces one in about 4 minutes, with every fact sourced and checked, for well under $1 of cost.

## Unit economics per memo

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Crustdata credits per memo | ~18 | **measured** (company record 2, ~10 searches, ~8 page fetches, minus cache hits) |
| Price per Crustdata credit | $0.02 | **assumption**: Crustdata doesn't publish a self-serve rate; replace with the rate on your plan |
| Data cost per memo | ~$0.36 | 18 × $0.02 |
| LLM tokens per memo | ~20–25k | **measured** (neatlogs trace totals, e.g. 21,602 tokens for Razorpay) |
| LLM cost per memo (paid list price) | ~$0.013 | **measured** at Gemini paid-tier list prices; $0 on free tiers |
| Compute per memo | ~$0.002 | t3.small at $0.0208/h, ~4 min per memo |
| **Total cost per memo** | **~$0.38** | |
| Time per memo | 3–5 min | **measured** |

## Pricing (assumption)

| Plan | Price | Includes | Cost to serve | Gross margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Angel | $49 / month | 25 memos, PDF export | 25 × $0.38 = $9.50 | ~81% |
| Fund | $399 / month | 300 memos, nightly watchlist, 5 seats, Slack digest | 300 × $0.38 = $114 | ~71% |
| Enterprise | from $2,000 / month | custom sources, private deployment, SSO, SLA | ~$500 | ~75% |
| Overage | $1.50 / memo | | $0.38 | ~75% |

## Fixed monthly costs (assumption)

| Item | Month 1–6 | Month 7–12 |
|---|---|---|
| Hosting (EC2 + storage + backups) | $60 | $250 |
| Tooling (neatlogs Pro, GitHub, email, domain) | $150 | $300 |
| Founder salary | $0 (bootstrapped) | $4,000 |
| First hire (engineer, from month 7) | – | $6,000 |
| Marketing | $300 | $1,500 |
| **Total** | **~$510** | **~$12,050** |

## Revenue scenario (assumption, to stress-test in cfo.ai)

| Month | Angel | Fund | Enterprise | MRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 | 0 | 0 | $245 |
| 3 | 25 | 3 | 0 | $2,422 |
| 6 | 60 | 10 | 1 | $8,930 |
| 9 | 110 | 22 | 2 | $18,168 |
| 12 | 160 | 35 | 4 | $29,805 |

5. "Should the Angel plan be $49 or $79? Compare 12-month revenue assuming 30% fewer Angel signups at $79."

Export or screenshot the model, the runway chart and Ari's answers into `business/` for the submission.

Here's where things stand.

**Step 1, before/after numbers (running).** The v2 eval is 2 of 12 companies in, about 50 minutes to go. The first comparison, fixed pipeline vs agent v1, is honest and mixed:
- **Better:** coverage 87% → 91%, every claim grounded in a source (98% → 100%), half the Crustdata credits (19 → 10 per memo), and real source conflicts now flagged (0 → 0.17 per memo).
- **Worse:** facts right on the answer key dropped from 92% to 81.5%.

That accuracy drop is exactly what the Coach targeted with its v2 prompt changes. When the eval finishes I'll fill the README results, write the Coach notes, and update the demo script and posts with the real numbers. If v2 doesn't beat v1, we say so; the Coach rejecting a bad change is also a good story for the theme.

**Step 4, business plan.** I updated `business/PLAN.md` with measured costs: about $0.26 per memo, 81–87% gross margin.

Good, the site is live. Here's the catch, and the plan:

**The catch:** GitHub Pages can only host fixed pages. It can't run the agent, and it must never hold your API keys. So "use it in the browser" needs a small server that runs Underwrite with your keys, plus limits so strangers can't burn your free credits. Rough capacity: your ~4,800 Crustdata credits ÷ ~10 per memo ≈ 400 memos.

**What I'll build:**
1. **Underwrite Live**, a web app in the same paper-dossier style. Anyone types a company name and website and presses Research. They watch the agents work live (searching, quoting, rejecting bad claims, the skeptic pushing back), then get the full dossier.
   - Companies already researched open instantly.
   - Limits: 2 new memos per visitor per day, a daily cap for the whole site, one job at a time with a queue.
2. **A "Try it live" button** on your current site that opens it.

One decision is yours, because it needs your account:

def run_company(company: str, domain: str | None, run_id: str, version: str | None = None,
                mode: str | None = None) -> CompanyState:
    """Run (or resume) one company. Never raises for agent failures: they're recorded in the state."""
    out = company_dir(run_id, company)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path, events_path = out / "state.json", out / "events.jsonl"
    state = load_state(path) or CompanyState(
        run_id=run_id, company=company, domain=domain, prompts_version=version or settings.prompts_version,
        mode=mode or settings.mode, started_at=time.time(),
    )
    if state.phase == "done":
        emit("info", f"{company}: already done, skipping")
        return state

    led = ledger.Ledger(**{k: v for k, v in (state.usage or {}).items() if k in ledger.Ledger.__dataclass_fields__})
    ltok, etok = ledger.bind(led), obs.bind_run(events_path)
    resumed = state.phase != "new"
    obs.console.rule(f"[bold]{company}[/bold] ({domain or 'no domain'}) · {state.mode} · prompts {state.prompts_version}"
                     + (f" · resuming at '{state.phase}'" if resumed else ""))
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        state.error = None
        with neatlogs.identify(session_id=run_id):
            _run(state, path, events_path, t0)
        m = state.metrics
        emit("memo", f"done in {m['duration_s']}s · {m['claims']} claims · {m['supported_rate']:.0%} supported · "
                     f"{m['conflicts']} conflicts · ${state.usage.get('llm_usd', 0):.3f} LLM · "
                     f"{state.usage.get('crust_credits', 0):g} Crustdata credits · {m['recoveries']} recoveries")
    except Exception as e:  # keep the batch going; the saved phase lets `resume` continue later
        state.error = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        emit("fail", f"{company}: stopped at phase '{state.phase}': {state.error}")
    finally:
        state.active_s += time.time() - t0
        state.usage = ledger.current().to_dict()
        path.write_text(state.model_dump_json(indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
        obs.unbind_run(etok)
        ledger.unbind(ltok)
    return state


def run_batch(companies: list[tuple[str, str | None]], run_id: str, version: str | None = None,
              mode: str | None = None) -> list[CompanyState]:
    manifest = settings.runs_dir / run_id / "manifest.json"
    manifest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    manifest.write_text(json.dumps({"run_id": run_id, "version": version or settings.prompts_version,
                                    "mode": mode or settings.mode, "companies": companies}, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    states: list[CompanyState] = []
    spent = 0.0
    for company, domain in companies:
        from .tools.crustdata import balance

        left = balance()
        low = left is not None and left < settings.min_credit_balance
        if low:
            emit("fail", f"Crustdata balance is {left:g} credits (< {settings.min_credit_balance:g} floor); not starting {company}")
        if spent >= settings.max_credits_per_run:
            emit("fail", f"credit cap reached ({spent:g} >= {settings.max_credits_per_run:g} Crustdata credits); "
                         f"skipping {company}. Raise UW_MAX_CREDITS_PER_RUN or resume later.")
        if low or spent >= settings.max_credits_per_run:
            states.append(load_state(company_dir(run_id, company) / "state.json") or CompanyState(
                run_id=run_id, company=company, domain=domain, prompts_version=version or settings.prompts_version,
                mode=mode or settings.mode, error="skipped: credit cap"))
            continue
        st = run_company(company, domain, run_id, version, mode)
        spent += float(st.usage.get("crust_credits", 0) or 0)
        states.append(st)
    neatlogs.flush()
    return states


def resume(run_id: str) -> list[CompanyState]:
    manifest = settings.runs_dir / run_id / "manifest.json"
    data = json.loads(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return run_batch([tuple(x) for x in data["companies"]], run_id, data.get("version"), data.get("mode", "pipeline"))

REPO_SSH="git@github.com:hacker-git-code/underwrite-.git"
APP="$HOME/underwrite"

sudo apt-get update -y
sudo apt-get install -y git curl ca-certificates fonts-dejavu

# Headless Chrome, used only to print memo dossiers to PDF.
if ! command -v google-chrome >/dev/null; then
  curl -fsSLo /tmp/chrome.deb https://dl.google.com/linux/direct/google-chrome-stable_current_amd64.deb
  sudo apt-get install -y /tmp/chrome.deb
fi

# uv: Python toolchain + locked dependencies.
command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Deploy key: write access to this one repository only (not your GitHub account).
mkdir -p ~/.ssh && chmod 700 ~/.ssh
if [ ! -f ~/.ssh/underwrite_deploy ]; then
  ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -f ~/.ssh/underwrite_deploy -C "underwrite-ec2"
  echo
  echo "Add this PUBLIC key in GitHub: repo Settings -> Deploy keys -> Add deploy key -> tick 'Allow write access':"
  echo
  cat ~/.ssh/underwrite_deploy.pub
  echo
  read -rp "Press Enter once the key is added... "
fi
cat > ~/.ssh/config <<'EOF'
Host github.com
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/underwrite_deploy
  IdentitiesOnly yes
EOF
chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config
ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 github.com >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts 2>/dev/null

cd "$APP"
uv sync

if [ ! -f .env ]; then

class Judgements(BaseModel):
    judgements: list[Judgement]


class MemoOut(BaseModel):
    recommendation: str
    confidence: Literal["low", "medium", "high"]
    memo_markdown: str
    fact_sheet: dict[str, str | int | float | list[str] | None] = Field(default_factory=dict)


# ---- persisted state ---------------------------------------------------------------


class Evidence(BaseModel):
    id: str
    kind: Literal["crustdata", "page", "snippet"]
    url: str | None = None
    title: str = ""
    text: str
    via: str  # crustdata | crustdata-web | ddg | direct
    question_ids: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    round: int = 1


class Claim(ExtractedClaim):
    id: str
    round: int = 1
    quote_found: bool = False
    quote_score: float = 0.0
    support: Literal["supported", "partial", "unsupported", "unchecked"] = "unchecked"
    reason: str = ""


class Conflict(BaseModel):
    field: str
    claims: list[str]  # claim ids
    values: list[str]
    note: str


class Objection(BaseModel):
    question_id: str = ""
    issue: str
    action: str = ""


class Review(BaseModel):
    verdict: Literal["ready", "needs_work"]
    objections: list[Objection] = Field(default_factory=list)


class CompanyState(BaseModel):
    run_id: str
    company: str
    domain: str | None = None
    prompts_version: str
    # "agent": analyst tool loop + skeptic review. "pipeline": the original fixed plan->search->extract->verify flow.
    mode: Literal["agent", "pipeline"] = "pipeline"
    # pipeline: new -> planned -> researched -> extracted -> verified -> written -> done
    # agent:    new -> planned -> investigating -> judging -> reviewing -> (investigating ...) -> writing -> written -> done
    phase: str = "new"
    round: int = 1
    question_status: dict[str, dict] = Field(default_factory=dict)  # qid -> {"status": open|answered|unanswerable, "note"}
    agent_messages: list[dict] = Field(default_factory=list)  # the analyst's conversation, checkpointed every step
    agent_steps: int = 0
    round_start_step: int = 0
    tasks_round: int = 1  # last round whose skeptic objections were handed to the analyst
    tool_counts: dict[str, int] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    claim_attempts: int = 0
    rejected_in_loop: int = 0
    self_corrections: int = 0
    reviews: list[Review] = Field(default_factory=list)
    active_s: float = 0.0  # time actually spent working (excludes time the process was not running)
    # set on watch runs: {"since": ts, "previous_run": id, "changes": [...], "headlines": [...]}
    watch: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)
    plan: Plan | None = None
    evidence: list[Evidence] = Field(default_factory=list)
    searched: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    fetched: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    claims: list[Claim] = Field(default_factory=list)
    conflicts: list[Conflict] = Field(default_factory=list)
    memo: MemoOut | None = None
    invalid_citations: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    metrics: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)
    usage: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)
    trace_ids: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    error: str | None = None
    started_at: float | None = None
    finished_at: float | None = None

# Running Underwrite unattended on AWS EC2

The website on GitHub Pages is static. A small EC2 instance runs the agent every night, adds the new memos to
`docs/`, and pushes. Nobody has to be watching: that is the point.

**Cost:** a t3.small is about $0.02/hour (~$0.50/day) plus ~$0.05/day for a 20 GB disk. Running it for the whole
hackathon and judging week costs a few dollars of the $25 allowance. Stop it when you're done.

## 1. Launch the instance (AWS console, logged in with the hackathon IAM user)

1. Region **US East (N. Virginia) us-east-1** (top-right).
2. EC2 → **Launch instance**:
   - Name: `underwrite-runner`
   - AMI: **Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS**
   - Instance type: **t3.small** (allowed: t2/t3/t3a, nano to large)
   - Key pair: create one (`underwrite-key`, .pem) and keep the file private
   - Network: **Hackathon_VPC**, any public subnet, **auto-assign public IP: enable**
   - Security group: inbound **SSH (22) from My IP only**. Nothing else.
   - Storage: 20 GB gp3 (limit is 50 GB)
   - No IAM instance profile is needed.
3. Launch. Only **one instance per IAM user** is allowed; terminate an old one before launching another.

## 2. Connect and set up

EC2 → your instance → **Connect** → **EC2 Instance Connect** → Connect (opens a terminal in the browser). Then:

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hacker-git-code/underwrite-/main/deploy/setup.sh
bash setup.sh
```

The script prints an SSH **public** key. Add it in GitHub → this repo → **Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key**,
tick **Allow write access**, save, and press Enter in the terminal. (A deploy key can only push to this one repo.)

Then put your keys on the server:

```bash
cd ~/underwrite && nano .env      # paste GEMINI_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, CRUSTDATA_API_KEY, NEATLOGS_API_KEY
uv run underwrite doctor          # every line should say ok / key set
~/underwrite/deploy/nightly.sh    # first run now; afterwards it runs every night at 02:00 IST
```

## 3. Keeping keys safe

- `.env` is created with `chmod 600` (only the `ubuntu` user can read it) and is git-ignored.
- The instance has no IAM role, so even a compromised process has no AWS credentials to steal; the agent's
  direct page fetcher also refuses non-public addresses such as the instance metadata service.
- SSH is open to your IP only. The deploy key can push to this repository and nothing else.
- When the hackathon is over: **terminate the instance**, delete the deploy key in GitHub, and rotate the API keys.

## 4. Watching it

```bash
tail -f ~/underwrite-nightly.log     # what the last run did
crontab -l                           # the schedule
```

Each night's commit (`nightly: unattended run …`) shows up in the repo history, and the traces in neatlogs.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Underwrite Live on this EC2 instance: the public web app behind Caddy, with automatic HTTPS.
# Run after setup.sh, as the 'ubuntu' user:   bash ~/underwrite/deploy/web.sh
# The instance's security group must allow inbound HTTP (80) and HTTPS (443) from anywhere.
# No domain needed: the address is <public-ip-with-dashes>.sslip.io (set UW_HOST to use your own domain).
set -euo pipefail

APP="$HOME/underwrite"
IP="$(curl -fsS https://checkip.amazonaws.com | tr -d '[:space:]')"
HOST="${UW_HOST:-${IP//./-}.sslip.io}"
PROMPTS="${UW_PROMPTS:-$(grep -E '^UW_PROMPTS=' "$APP/.env" 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f2 || true)}"
PROMPTS="${PROMPTS:-v1}"

# Caddy: reverse proxy that gets and renews a Let's Encrypt certificate by itself.
if ! command -v caddy >/dev/null; then
  sudo apt-get install -y debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https gnupg
  curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key' | sudo gpg --dearmor --yes -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
  curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list >/dev/null
  sudo apt-get update -y
  sudo apt-get install -y caddy
fi
sudo tee /etc/caddy/Caddyfile >/dev/null <<EOF
$HOST {
	encode gzip
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8080 {
		flush_interval -1
	}
}
EOF
sudo systemctl reload caddy || sudo systemctl restart caddy

# The app as a service: starts on boot, restarts if it crashes; queued jobs resume from their checkpoints.
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/underwrite-web.service >/dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=Underwrite Live
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
User=$USER
WorkingDirectory=$APP
Environment=PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
Environment=UW_PROMPTS=$PROMPTS
ExecStart=$HOME/.local/bin/uv run underwrite serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now underwrite-web
sudo systemctl restart underwrite-web

echo
echo "Underwrite Live is starting at:  https://$HOST"
echo "(the HTTPS certificate takes up to a minute the first time)"
echo "Logs:  journalctl -u underwrite-web -f"

## 2b. Underwrite Live: let anyone use it from their browser

The same instance can host the public web app (type a company, watch the agents work, get the dossier). It needs
the web ports open: EC2 → your instance → **Security** tab → the security group → **Edit inbound rules** → add
**HTTP (80)** and **HTTPS (443)** from **Anywhere-IPv4**. Then, in the instance terminal:

```bash
cd ~/underwrite && git pull && uv sync
bash deploy/web.sh                 # prints the address, e.g. https://3-80-1-2.sslip.io

`underwrite serve` as a systemd service that restarts on crashes and reboots; a job that was running resumes from
its checkpoint. Free-use limits, all in `.env`: `UW_WEB_PER_VISITOR` (default 2 new memos per visitor per day),
`UW_WEB_DAILY_CAP` (25 per day for the whole site), `UW_WEB_MAX_QUEUE` (8), plus the Crustdata balance floor
`UW_MIN_CREDIT_BALANCE`. Companies researched in the last 30 days open instantly and cost nothing.

## 3. Keeping keys safe

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Running Underwrite unattended on AWS EC2

The website on GitHub Pages is static. A small EC2 instance runs the agent every night, adds the new memos to
`docs/`, and pushes. Nobody has to be watching: that is the point.

**Cost:** a t3.small is about $0.02/hour (~$0.50/day) plus ~$0.05/day for a 20 GB disk. Running it for the whole
hackathon and judging week costs a few dollars of the $25 allowance. Stop it when you're done.

## 1. Launch the instance (AWS console, logged in with the hackathon IAM user)

1. Region **US East (N. Virginia) us-east-1** (top-right).
2. EC2 → **Launch instance**:
   - Name: `underwrite-runner`
   - AMI: **Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS**
   - Instance type: **t3.small** (allowed: t2/t3/t3a, nano to large)
   - Key pair: create one (`underwrite-key`, .pem) and keep the file private
   - Network: **Hackathon_VPC**, any public subnet, **auto-assign public IP: enable**
   - Security group: inbound **SSH (22) from My IP only**. Nothing else.
   - Storage: 20 GB gp3 (limit is 50 GB)
   - No IAM instance profile is needed.
3. Launch. Only **one instance per IAM user** is allowed; terminate an old one before launching another.

## 2. Connect and set up

EC2 → your instance → **Connect** → **EC2 Instance Connect** → Connect (opens a terminal in the browser). Then:

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hacker-git-code/underwrite-/main/deploy/setup.sh
bash setup.sh
```

The script prints an SSH **public** key. Add it in GitHub → this repo → **Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key**,
tick **Allow write access**, save, and press Enter in the terminal. (A deploy key can only push to this one repo.)

Then put your keys on the server:

```bash
cd ~/underwrite && nano .env      # paste GEMINI_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, CRUSTDATA_API_KEY, NEATLOGS_API_KEY
uv run underwrite doctor          # every line should say ok / key set
~/underwrite/deploy/nightly.sh    # first run now; afterwards it runs every night at 02:00 IST
```

## 2b. Underwrite Live: let anyone use it from their browser

The same instance can host the public web app (type a company, watch the agents work, get the dossier). It needs
the web ports open: EC2 → your instance → **Security** tab → the security group → **Edit inbound rules** → add
**HTTP (80)** and **HTTPS (443)** from **Anywhere-IPv4**. Then, in the instance terminal:

```bash
cd ~/underwrite && git pull && uv sync
bash deploy/web.sh                 # prints the address, e.g. https://3-80-1-2.sslip.io
```

`deploy/web.sh` installs Caddy (automatic HTTPS from Let's Encrypt, no domain needed thanks to sslip.io) and runs
`underwrite serve` as a systemd service that restarts on crashes and reboots; a job that was running resumes from
its checkpoint. Free-use limits, all in `.env`: `UW_WEB_PER_VISITOR` (default 2 new memos per visitor per day),
`UW_WEB_DAILY_CAP` (25 per day for the whole site), `UW_WEB_MAX_QUEUE` (8), plus the Crustdata balance floor
`UW_MIN_CREDIT_BALANCE`. Companies researched in the last 30 days open instantly and cost nothing.

## 3. Keeping keys safe

- `.env` is created with `chmod 600` (only the `ubuntu` user can read it) and is git-ignored.
- The instance has no IAM role, so even a compromised process has no AWS credentials to steal; the agent's
  direct page fetcher also refuses non-public addresses such as the instance metadata service.
- SSH is open to your IP only. The deploy key can push to this repository and nothing else.
- When the hackathon is over: **terminate the instance**, delete the deploy key in GitHub, and rotate the API keys.

## 4. Watching it

```bash
tail -f ~/underwrite-nightly.log     # what the last run did
crontab -l                           # the schedule
```

Each night's commit (`nightly: unattended run …`) shows up in the repo history, and the traces in neatlogs.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The unattended job: research the next few companies on the watchlist, rebuild the website,
# and publish it. Safe to re-run: finished companies are skipped, unfinished ones resume.
set -euo pipefail
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

echo "=== nightly run $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) ==="
git pull --rebase --autostash
uv sync --quiet

# 3 new companies a night keeps Crustdata use around 60 credits/night.
uv run underwrite batch deploy/watchlist.txt --new-only --limit "${UW_NIGHTLY_LIMIT:-3}"
# Re-check what we already covered: refresh the record, scan news since the memo, re-investigate only real changes.
uv run underwrite watch --limit "${UW_WATCH_LIMIT:-5}"
uv run underwrite site

git add docs runs
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "nothing new to publish"
else
  git commit -m "nightly: unattended run $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ)"
  git push
fi

flagging real disagreements between sources, but cost accuracy on the answer key. The Coach read the agents'

lost accuracy there, but it answered fewer questions and dipped on the training companies. **Its own gate judges on
the training split, so it rejected v2 and v1 stays in production.** An agent that won't ship its own change because
one number got worse is the behaviour we want from something that runs unattended. Details:
[prompts/v2/COACH_NOTES.md](prompts/v2/COACH_NOTES.md).

content.content:
1 # Underwrite 2 3 **A team of AI agents that does venture due diligence while you sleep, and checks its own work.** 4 Give it a list of startups. # neatHack 2026 — Underwrite

## Project

**Underwrite** — an autonomous due-diligence agent you can leave running overnight.
Give it a list of startups; it plans the research, pulls company data from Crustdata,
searches and reads the web, extracts every factual claim with a source, has an
independent verifier check each claim against the source text, flags contradictions
(e.g. "website says 50 people, Crustdata says 18"), and writes a cited investment memo
as a three-page paper dossier (HTML, PDF, PNG).

A **Coach** loop reads the agent's own neatlogs traces, detections and triage fixes
over the neatlogs MCP server, rewrites the agent's prompts, re-runs the eval set,
and only keeps a change if the numbers improve.

- Challenge: "Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching." (single track)
- Required tools: neatlogs (tracing + Coach loop), Entire (checkpointed build sessions), cfo.ai (business plan)
- Repo: https://github.com/hacker-git-code/underwrite-
- Live site: https://hacker-git-code.github.io/underwrite-/ (after GitHub Pages is enabled)

## Team

- Rehan Momin (solo)

## Stack

- Python 3.12, uv
- LLMs (free tiers): Gemini 3.8 Flash / 3.5 Flash / 3.5 Flash-Lite / 3.1 Flash-Lite, Groq gpt-oss-120b / 20b;
  Claude on Bedrock supported but not used (the AWS allowance covers EC2/Lambda only)
- Data: Crustdata (company enrich, web search, web fetch, credit balance)
- Observability: neatlogs Python SDK + neatlogs MCP (Coach)
- Build provenance: Entire CLI (checkpoints on every commit, secrets redacted)
- Hosting: GitHub Pages (site) + AWS EC2 t3.small (nightly runner)

## Build log

### 2026-10-10

- Read hackathon page, neatlogs SDK/MCP docs, Entire CLI README, Crustdata API docs.
- Chose idea: due-diligence agent + self-improving Coach loop.
- Installed Entire CLI 0.11.4, `git init`, `entire enable --agent claude-code`.
- Built v0 (commit `5b0a6b0`): planner → researcher → extractor → verifier → replanner → writer; checkpointed
  state machine with `resume`; chaos mode; eval harness (12 companies, train/test split); Coach over neatlogs MCP.
- Found the AWS check-in page only approves EC2/Lambda/IAM/LB, not Bedrock → switched LLMs to free Gemini + Groq
  behind a provider fallback chain (commit `56d3dc2`). Gemini 2.5 models are closed to new keys → Gemini 3.x defaults.
- First real run (Razorpay): accurate but thin; found the search budget was spent on 4 of 8 questions. Fixed with
  breadth-first queries + 2 searches reserved for the gap round (commit `ab59efd`). Re-run: 9/9 topics, 12 claims, 92% supported.
- Crustdata record was 4,291 lines (mostly executives' employment history) → curated 34-line summary.
- Memo redesigned as a paper dossier modelled on Sequoia's 1977 Apple evaluation form (commit `e06539d`).
- Security pass: SSRF guard, prompt-injection guard, HTML escaping, credit cap + live balance floor, model cooldowns;
  scanned git history, tracked files and Entire checkpoints for key values: none found (Entire redacts secrets).
- Pushed to GitHub; added website (`docs/`), EC2 nightly runner (`deploy/`), business plan, demo script, post drafts.
- v1 baseline eval running (12 companies).
- Tests: `tests/test_offline.py` 6/6 pass (pipeline, resume after crash, chaos recovery, fact scoring, SSRF, HTML escaping).

## Demo

- Script: `submission/DEMO_SCRIPT.md` (video pending)

## Evidence checklist (from the hackathon page)

- [ ] Before/after run comparison with numbers — after the Coach run (`prompts/v2/COACH_NOTES.md`)
- [x] neatlogs trace links / screenshots — trace ids printed per run and in each dossier appendix
- [x] Entire checkpoints from the repo — `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers, refs pushed to GitHub
- [ ] cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway) — inputs ready in `business/PLAN.md`
- [x] A run where an action failed and the agent recovered — `[recover]` events in every real run so far
  (Crustdata ConnectError → retry, empty pages → direct fetch, malformed JSON → repair, Gemini 503 → retry)
- [ ] Public posts tagged #neatHack — drafts in `submission/POSTS.md`
- [x] Public repo with commits dated during the hackathon

## Limitations & next steps

- Ground truth covers stable facts only; judgement quality isn't auto-scored.
- Free-tier LLM quotas limit batch size per day.

## Submission status

- Not submitted. Submissions open Mon 12 Oct, 7:00–11:55 PM IST (quote-tweet the official neatlogs post).

Judging weights the video at 20% ("how clearly it explains the agent and the tool use") and the agent itself at 30%,
so the video is built around **watching the agents make decisions**. Record at 1080p, terminal font ≥ 16pt.

**Before recording, open in tabs:** the live site · one agent dossier (Ramp) · its neatlogs trace · GitHub commits ·
`prompts/v2/COACH_NOTES.md` · `submission/ENTIRE.md` · the cfo.ai model. Warm the cache once:
`uv run underwrite run "Ramp" --domain ramp.com --chaos 0.2`.

|---|---|---|

Pause on `[agent] step N -> web_search(...)`, then a `REJECTED` line and the `self-corrected` line | "The analyst agent decides every move: pull the **Crustdata** record, search, read a page, record a claim. | 0:45–1:05 | Pause on `[skeptic] objection…` and `sending the analyst back` | "Then a skeptic agent attacks the work: 'your traction numbers come from one blog, and you never checked risks.' Everything is live and pushed.

**What anyone can use now:**
- **https://184-73-13-58.sslip.io** is the free app on your AWS server. Anyone types a startup, presses RESEARCH IT, and watches the agents work live, then gets the dossier. It's HTTPS and runs 24/7. I tested it with Vercel: 16 of 16 facts verified, 2 bad quotes thrown out, 5.6 minutes.
- **Your site** (hacker-git-code.github.io/underwrite-) now has a red **TRY IT LIVE →** button that opens it.
- **Limits that keep your credits safe:** 2 new memos per person per day and 15 per day for the whole site. Companies already researched open instantly for free. You have 4,636 Crustdata credits left.
- **One thing to know:** the free Gemini quota resets every day around 12:30 PM IST. If it runs low, the app falls back to other models, so it keeps working, just a bit slower.

**The 4 steps:**
1. **Before/after numbers: done.** On companies the Coach never saw, v2 got 80% of facts right (up from 67%) and 98% of claims were backed by their source (up from 82%). But it answered fewer questions, so the Coach rejected its own change and v1 stays live. It's all in the README results table and `prompts/v2/COACH_NOTES.md`.
2. **Demo video: the script is ready** in `submission/DEMO_SCRIPT.md`, now opening with the live app. You record it.
3. **Posts: the texts are ready** in `submission/POSTS.md` with the real numbers and the live link. You post them with #neatHack.
4. **cfo.ai: still open.** The plan is updated with measured costs (about $0.26 per memo). Reply **"yes cfo"** and I'll enter it in your Chrome, or do it yourself from `business/PLAN.md`.

**Two notes:**
- The server costs about $0.50 a day from your $25 AWS credit. Stop it after judging (EC2 → Instance state → Stop).
- The README says the server also researches new companies every night. That part isn't switched on yet, because it needs a GitHub deploy key. If you want it, I'll create the key on the server and you paste it into GitHub (1 minute). Otherwise I'll remove that line so the README stays accurate.
